| Contract development | 0.70 | 0.38 | 46% | S1 (unverified) |
| Total | 2.60 | 1.09 | 58% | S1 (unverified) |

FY2025 revenue of $2.6M, company-reported and unverified, is $1.1M evaluation, $0.8M research-use and $0.7M development. The volumes in the table are reconstructions, not disclosures: at $33.40 and $16.20, $1.10M of evaluation revenue implies about 20,160 cartridges only if the $650 fee were charged on all 55 analyzers for twelve months ($0.43M, an upper bound), and the 58% is the deck's total, so line costs are allocations and the bridge does not close by line. The reconstruction cannot be squared with the deck's shipment total: 27,600 cartridges shipped since March 2024 average 890 a month over 31 months, and at the January-September 2026 average of 1,680 a month, nine months consume 15,120, leaving 12,480 — 567 a month — for the 22 months to December 2025. A FY2025 of 20,160 evaluation plus 23,952 research-use cartridges, 44,112, exceeds the entire 27,600; either the cumulative counts only part of the business, or the revenue mix is misstated, or the evaluation line carries revenue beyond fees and cartridges. The 1.22 panels a day is a January-September 2026 figure only, and utilisation carries low confidence until a monthly shipment ledger arrives. Normalised FY2026E revenue is $3.5M after removing the $2.4M stocking order: $2.7M in nine months plus $0.8M in Q4; on flat per-analyzer use, the $0.9M increase over FY2025 must come from more analyzers, research-use or development revenue. With the largest customer at 15% and the development partner at 27%, the top two relationships are 42% [S1].

### The clinic's margin rests on the one assay that carries 55% of the payment

CMS's CY2026 Clinical Laboratory Fee Schedule national limitation amounts:

| Test (CPT code) | CY2026 amount | Source |

| Troponin, quantitative (84484) | $12.47 | S154; S180 |

| Creatinine (82570) | $5.18 | S154; S180 |

Against the $33.40 realised price a five-code clinic keeps $37.98 a panel and Vantelle takes 47% of the Medicare payment; at the $38 list the clinic keeps $33.38 and the fee equals 19.5 panels. Natriuretic peptide alone is $39.26, 55% of it: a clinic billing four codes without that assay collects $32.12 and loses $1.28 a cartridge, and troponin plus potassium collects $17.23 and loses $16.17. At 30.5 panels a month the five-code clinic earns $1,158.39 and keeps $508.39 after the $650 fee — the fee equals 17.1 panels — and $8,465.20 at 240 panels: trivial at scale, 56% of the margin at adoption. CMS may cut a test by up to 15% a year in 2027-2029, and three such years would take this panel to $43.84 and the clinic's spread to $10.44 [S154, S180].

| Vantelle Q5 cartridge, five assays | $38.00 list; $33.40 realised | $7.60 per analyte at list | S1 (unverified) |

| Quidel Triage Troponin, 25 tests | $599 | $23.96 | S106 |
| Quidel Triage MeterPro | Free with three-year contract | — | S106 |

### 92% reorder is engagement, not demand

Thirty-four of 37 sites reordered within 90 days, company-reported and unverified. The 37 are the sites in the programme at least 90 days; four are too new to qualify. Whether the three reordered later is not disclosed. No site can become a paying commercial customer before clearance, so no lost-deal evidence exists yet; the first will come from the 300-site distributor pipeline. At 41 cartridges a site a month a reorder is one month of consumption: the metric shows repeat use at a price already accepted, not commercial demand. ## Mandatory Evidence Gate

| Required item | Minimum standard |
| --- | --- |

| Primary/source-of-truth check | At least 1 primary or near-primary source where available: filing, company page, registry, patent, investor announcement, regulatory record, official report, customer/procurement record. |
| Mechanism | Explain how the evidence changes economics, adoption, pricing power, risk, financing need, valuation, or exit probability. A fact without mechanism is not analysis. |
| Public-equity source-of-truth | For listed companies, use primary filings or company IR for financial statements and record market data timestamp, exchange, currency, latest price, market cap, and enterprise value if available. |

| Comparison | At least 1 competitor, benchmark, base rate, industry norm, or historical comparable. |
| Counter-evidence | At least 1 contradicting source, weakness, adverse case, or reason the thesis may fail. |
| Investor implication | A decision-relevant conclusion: invest, pass, wait, lower valuation, add condition, or request diligence. |

arguments.markdown:
The revenue model is a $2,900 analyzer that costs $3,350 to build and a $38 consumable cartridge it realises $33.40 on, and it only clears its own costs at four to six panels per analyzer per day — four to six times what its 55 evaluation analyzers run. That gap decides whether the $78.5M of 2029 revenue exists. Figures are company-reported and unverified. The only dated volume is 1,680 cartridges a month, the January-September 2026 average (p.7, headed "2026 average", as of 2026-09-30); across 55 analyzers that is 30.5 cartridge-months, 1.0 panel a day (1.22 on 300 operating days), against 8.0 in 2028 [S1].

### The razor loses money twice before the blade earns anything

Under this revenue model each placement is subsidised twice, company-reported and unverified. Build cost is $3,350 against a $2,900 list, and 60% of evaluation sites received their analyzer free, so an average placement realises $1,160 against $3,350 of cost — a $2,190 cash subsidy. The deck does not say how the analyzer is accounted for: the 58% margin needs the $184,250 cost of 55 analyzers outside cost of sales; expensing it gives 51%, three-year capitalisation 56%. The cartridge earns $17.20 at $33.40 against $16.20 cost, a 51.5% gross margin, less a 3% royalty to Corvia Microfluidics, the 60%-owned affiliate whose 22% minority holder is the chief technology officer; that royalty is $1.00 a cartridge today and $2.35M a year at the 2029 plan — a related-party claim. $7.50 at two million cartridges is a 54% cut from $16.20 on a line running 1,680 a month — a redesign, not a learning curve. Nine sales and support staff placed 55 analyzers in 31 months; at $120,000-240,000 fully loaded and half charged to placements, CAC is $25,600-51,200 [S1]. Three years of cartridge gross profit less the $2,190 subsidy, $15,621, does not repay that; it turns positive at 5.9 panels a day at today's cost and 4.2 at the $7.50 target, where a three-year LTV:CAC reaches 3:1.

| Line | 2026 actual | 2028 model | 2029 target | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Cartridges per analyzer-month | 30.5 | 200 | 200 | S1 (unverified); calculated |
| Panels per analyzer-day | 1.0 (1.22 on 300 days) | 8.0 | 8.0 | S1 (unverified); calculated |
| Realised cartridge price | $33.40 | $31.00 | $31.00 | S1 (unverified) |
| Cartridge cost | $16.20 | $10.23 | $7.50 | S1 (unverified) |
| Annual cartridge gross profit per analyzer | $5,937 | $47,616 | $54,168 | S1 (unverified); calculated |
| Three-year cartridge LTV less subsidy | $15,621 | $140,658 | $160,314 | S1 (unverified); calculated |
| LTV:CAC, cartridges only | 0.3-0.6x | 2.7-5.5x | 3.1-6.3x | S1 (unverified); calculated |

### FY2025 revenue is three businesses, and its volume is not disclosed

| FY2025 line | Revenue $M | Cost $M | Gross margin | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Evaluation: fees and cartridges | 1.10 | 0.33 | 70% | S1 (unverified); calculated |
| Research-use | 0.80 | 0.39 | 51% | S1 (unverified); calculated |
| Contract development | 0.70 | 0.38 | 46% | S1 (unverified) |
| Total | 2.60 | 1.09 | 58% | S1 (unverified) |

FY2025 revenue of $2.6M, company-reported and unverified, is $1.1M evaluation, $0.8M research-use and $0.7M development. The volumes in the table are reconstructions, not disclosures: at $33.40 and $16.20, $1.10M of evaluation revenue implies about 20,160 cartridges only if the $650 fee were charged on all 55 analyzers for twelve months ($0.43M, an upper bound), and the 58% is the deck's total, so line costs are allocations and the bridge does not close by line. The reconstruction cannot be squared with the deck's shipment total: 27,600 cartridges shipped since March 2024 average 890 a month over 31 months, and at the January-September 2026 average of 1,680 a month, nine months consume 15,120, leaving 12,480 — 567 a month — for the 22 months to December 2025. A FY2025 of 20,160 evaluation plus 23,952 research-use cartridges, 44,112, exceeds the entire 27,600; either the cumulative counts only part of the business, or the revenue mix is misstated, or the evaluation line carries revenue beyond fees and cartridges. The 1.22 panels a day is a January-September 2026 figure only, and utilisation carries low confidence until a monthly shipment ledger arrives. Normalised FY2026E revenue is $3.5M after removing the $2.4M stocking order: $2.7M in nine months plus $0.8M in Q4; on flat per-analyzer use, the $0.9M increase over FY2025 must come from more analyzers, research-use or development revenue. With the largest customer at 15% and the development partner at 27%, the top two relationships are 42% [S1].

### The clinic's margin rests on the one assay that carries 55% of the payment

CMS's CY2026 Clinical Laboratory Fee Schedule national limitation amounts:

| Test (CPT code) | CY2026 amount | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Troponin, quantitative (84484) | $12.47 | S154; S180 |
| Natriuretic peptide (83880) | $39.26 | S154; S180 |
| Haemoglobin A1c (83036) | $9.71 | S154; S180 |
| Creatinine (82570) | $5.18 | S154; S180 |
| Potassium (84132) | $4.76 | S154; S180 |
| Five-code panel | $71.38 | S154; S180 |

Against the $33.40 realised price a five-code clinic keeps $37.98 a panel and Vantelle takes 47% of the Medicare payment; at the $38 list the clinic keeps $33.38 and the fee equals 19.5 panels. Natriuretic peptide alone is $39.26, 55% of it: a clinic billing four codes without that assay collects $32.12 and loses $1.28 a cartridge, and troponin plus potassium collects $17.23 and loses $16.17. At 30.5 panels a month the five-code clinic earns $1,158.39 and keeps $508.39 after the $650 fee — the fee equals 17.1 panels — and $8,465.20 at 240 panels: trivial at scale, 56% of the margin at adoption. CMS may cut a test by up to 15% a year in 2027-2029, and three such years would take this panel to $43.84 and the clinic's spread to $10.44 [S154, S180].

| Product or fee | Price | Per test or analyte | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| Vantelle Q5 cartridge, five assays | $38.00 list; $33.40 realised | $7.60 per analyte at list | S1 (unverified) |
| Vantelle evaluation fee | $650 per analyzer-month | 17.1 panels of clinic margin at observed use | S1 (unverified) |
| Quidel Triage Troponin, 25 tests | $599 | $23.96 | S106 |
| Quidel Triage MeterPro | Free with three-year contract | — | S106 |

### 92% reorder is engagement, not demand

Thirty-four of 37 sites reordered within 90 days, company-reported and unverified. The 37 are the sites in the programme at least 90 days; four are too new. Whether the three reordered later is not disclosed. No site can become a paying commercial customer before clearance, so no lost-deal evidence exists yet; the first will come from the 300-site distributor pipeline. At 41 cartridges a site a month a reorder is one month of consumption: the metric shows repeat use at a price already accepted, not commercial demand. Per site the run rate is 1.35 panels a day against a median of 14 cardiac or metabolic panels sent out daily at the 52 clinics Vantelle surveyed — 10% capture. The plan needs two analyzers at eight panels each, 16 a site, 114% of that median: the model assumes the panel replaces the entire send-out, not the urgent slice. Reaching 300 sites by end-2027 means 259 net adds in twelve months, 21.6 a month against 1.3 a month averaged since March 2024, 402 analyzers and about 1.16M cartridges a year — 57 times the January-September 2026 average of 1,680 — from an 18-person line [S1].

Counter-evidence: evaluation analyzers are investigational, results never reach patient care, and no site has a billing reason to run more. A clinic that collects the full panel reimbursement has an incentive no evaluation site has, and the survey's latent send-out volume makes a modest panel count credible; the plan's is not, until a billing-enabled site demonstrates it. Underwrite panels per analyzer-day, with the site count a milestone, and test the monthly fee against a free-instrument, minimum-volume alternative. Confidence is high on the arithmetic and medium on the interpretation: evaluation data cannot distinguish a floor from a ceiling. Three diligence items: the best evaluation site's monthly volume; the first billing-enabled sites' run rate; and panel mix, since troponin plus potassium alone do not cover a cartridge.

::: evidence
**A placement runs one panel a day, not eight; at CMS's CY2026 rates the five-code clinic keeps $508.39 a month.**
55 analyzers consumed 1,680 cartridges a month, the January-September 2026 average, company-reported and unverified — 30.5 per analyzer-month against 240; the five-code panel pays $71.38 and the cartridge costs the clinic $33.40, so the $650 fee equals 17.1 panels of a $37.98 margin and a placement's $15,621 three-year gross profit does not repay an estimated $25,600-51,200 to win it [S1, S154]. The FY2025 line volumes do not reconcile with 27,600 cumulative shipments, so the 58% margin and the 1.22 rate carry low confidence until the shipment ledger arrives.
:::

arguments.markdown:
Vantelle has six months of cash, company-reported and unverified, and a $30M round that funds its own plan only into 2028. On the report's base — clearance in the second half of 2027, a waiver in 2028 and two to four panels a day — the company consumes $55-70M before breakeven, so $30M is a financing milestone, not the financing. It starts at $6.9M on 2026-09-30 and $1.15M a month [S1]: 6.0 months, exhaustion around 2027-03-30, and $2.3M — 2.0 months — left at the 2027-01-29 target close. That burn is the FY2026E net loss of $14.0M with no capex or working capital in it, so launch spending accelerates the date; a close six months late, on 2027-07-29, needs about $5.3M of bridge including the first Bluestem payments.

### The plan's operating leverage is real and rests on one variable

| Line item, $M | FY2024 | FY2025 | FY2026E | FY2027P | FY2028P | FY2029P | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Revenue | 1.1 | 2.6 | 5.9 | 16.8 | 41.0 | 78.5 | S1 (unverified) |
| Revenue growth | — | 136% | 127% | 185% | 144% | 91% | S1 (unverified); calculated |
| Gross margin | 49% | 58% | 61% | 63% | 67% | 71% | S1 (unverified) |
| Gross profit | 0.5 | 1.5 | 3.6 | 10.6 | 27.5 | 55.7 | S1 (unverified); calculated |
| Net loss | (9.8) | (12.4) | (14.0) | (16.5) | (6.0) | 9.0 | S1 (unverified) |
| Implied operating cost | 10.3 | 13.9 | 17.6 | 27.1 | 33.5 | 46.7 | S1 (unverified); calculated |

Implied operating cost — gross profit minus net loss — rises from $10.3M in FY2024 to $17.6M in FY2026E and $46.7M in FY2029P while revenue rises 13.3x, and that gap is the investment case. It also sets the target: at the 2029 margin of 71%, breakeven needs $65.8M of revenue — 884 analyzers running 2,400 panels a year at $31, or 660 sites at 1.34 analyzers each, twice the 300 sites targeted for end-2027. The deck's own $78.5M needs about 1,055 analyzers at eight panels a day, 2.6 times the 402 analyzers behind the 300-site plan. The cost target fails the same test: two million cartridges a year is what buys the $7.50 cost; at the 1.22 panels a day the 55 evaluation analyzers ran in the January-September 2026 average, an analyzer consumes about 360 cartridges a year, so that volume needs 5,500 analyzers, and the 402 analyzers behind the 300-site plan produce 147,000 cartridges, 7% of it, where the only disclosed cost is $16.20 and the margin 48%, not 76% [S1].

### Forty-one per cent of 2026 revenue cannot be delivered in 2026

Company-reported FY2026E revenue of $5.9M includes a $2.4M opening stocking order from Southwest Clinical Supply that ships only on 510(k) clearance, dated Q1 2027, under a non-binding LOI [S1]. At $33.40 a cartridge it is 71,856 cartridges — 42.8 months at the January-September 2026 average of 1,680 a month — for a product with six months of stability data behind a nine-month claim. Excluding it, FY2026 revenue is $3.5M; with $2.7M booked in nine months the fourth quarter is $0.8M against a $0.9M quarterly average, so the base business is not growing into the year-end. Gross margin makes the same point: 61% in FY2026E is above FY2025's 58% in the year the mix shifts toward a distributor, and a 30% wholesale discount would take the order's margin to 39% and the blend to 52%, cutting gross profit by $0.5M.

### Working capital and the term loan are missing from the use of funds

The launch consumes cash before it produces it, and the deck's use of funds has no working-capital line. At peer working-capital intensity — QuidelOrtho carried 55.7 receivable days and 145 inventory days in FY2025 — 2028 revenue of $41.0M and COGS of $13.5M imply $6.3M of receivables and $2.2-5.4M of inventory at 60-145 days, so $8-12M of working capital against near zero today; on the base's $15.0M of 2028 revenue the need is $3-5M [S1, S22]. The debt compounds the timing: the $5.0M Bluestem term loan is interest-only to 2027-03 and then amortises $166,667 a month for 30 months to 2029-09, with the rate and covenants not disclosed — at 10-12% interest is $42,000-50,000 a month, and debt service after 2027-03 is $210,000 a month, 18% of burn. It amortises whether or not the product is cleared. The $6.0M of bridge notes at 8% cost $40,000 a month and become $6.28M at close, converting at 75% of the $3.2564 round price into 2,571,392 shares, 4.9% of the post-round count.

| Metric | FY2025 | FY2026E | Benchmark | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Net margin | (477%) | (237%) | QuidelOrtho (41.5%) | S1 (unverified), S22 |
| Burn multiple | 8.3x | 4.2x, or 15.6x ex-stocking order | Series B median 1.4x | S1 (unverified), S134 |
| ROE and ROIC | not meaningful | not meaningful | Accumulated deficit above $36.2M against $40.5M of equity raised | S1 (unverified); calculated |
| Receivable days | not disclosed | not disclosed | QuidelOrtho 55.7 days | S22 |
| Inventory days | not disclosed | not disclosed | QuidelOrtho 145 days | S22 |

### The round covers the company's plan only if everything lands on time

In the deck's plan — Q1 2027 clearance, eight panels a day, $78.5M of 2029 revenue — $32.3M at close less 2027 outflows of $25.0M leaves $7.3M, and 2028's $12.0M outflow takes it to negative $4.7M: the trough arrives before the 2029 profit and the shortfall is $8-10M, so the plan needs $40M. That plan is not the report's base. The base assumes one more information cycle on S97's FY2024 average of 139 days total time to decision, putting clearance in H2 2027; revenue is $7.0M, $15.0M and $25.0M in 2027-2029, gross margin 52%, 58% and 63%, and operating cost $24M, $27M and $30M. The losses are $20.4M, $18.3M and $14.3M; with $8M of capex, $3M of working capital and $5M of principal, less $7.5M of depreciation, the cumulative outflow is $61M by end-2029 and about $68M to breakeven in 2031: the $55-70M range, against $32.3M at close, leaves $25-38M of new money — call it a $25-40M round — and 23-32% dilution at half the round price. A downside with clearance in H1 2028 or a refused waiver and one to two panels a day adds a further $40-50M and 35-42% dilution [S1, S97, S140].

| $M | Company plan (Q1 2027, 8 panels/day) | Report base (H2 2027, 2-4 panels/day) | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| Revenue, FY2027 / 2028 / 2029 | 16.8 / 41.0 / 78.5 | 7.0 / 15.0 / 25.0 | S1 (unverified); analyst estimate |
| Cash at close, 2027-01-29 | 32.3 | 32.3 | calculated |
| FY2027 outflow | 25.0 | 23.4 | calculated |
| FY2028 outflow | 12.0 | 22.3 | calculated |
| FY2029 | +9.5 inflow | 15.8 outflow | calculated |
| Trough | -4.7 in 2028 | -29.1 at end-2029 | calculated |
| Capital to breakeven | 40 | 55-70 | calculated |
| Additional beyond the round | 8-10 | 25-38 | calculated |

These are capital-intensive instrument economics: growth is bought with placed hardware and funded receivables, so the faster Vantelle sells, the more cash it burns before the cartridge annuity arrives. The variable that moves the outcome is panels per analyzer-day, not sites, price or the clearance date: clearance moves the clock, utilisation sets the level. At $31 a cartridge, the base's $25M of 2029 revenue is 806,000 cartridges — 896 analyzers at three panels a day, roughly 600 sites, twice the 300-site plan — which is why even the base consumes $55-70M. The counter-case is discretionary burn: cutting cost and slowing the site ramp would close most of the gap, and a distributor that finances inventory would remove much of the working-capital need, so the shortfall is about this plan, not survival. Capital efficiency is poor: the burn multiple is 8.3x in FY2025, 4.2x in FY2026E, 15.6x excluding the stocking order and 1.5x in FY2027P on the company plan, against a Series B median near 1.4x; on the base's $7.0M of 2027 revenue and $23.4M outflow it is 6.7x against normalised FY2026 revenue. Revenue per dollar of capital raised is $0.05 in FY2025 on $51.5M, and $0.21 in FY2027P on $81.5M including the round — $4.85 of capital per dollar of 2027 revenue on the company plan and $11.6 on the base. Size the round larger or tranche it on clearance and utilisation, and price for a further financing before breakeven. Diligence: the Bluestem rate, covenants and minimum-cash test; the distributor's payment, return and pricing terms; and the Tempe line's cost and yield at launch volumes. Confidence is high on the arithmetic, which reconciles to the deck, and medium on the projections, which are unaudited management estimates with no auditor, quarterly statements or covenant disclosure.

::: info danger
**The largest single line of FY2026 revenue cannot be delivered in FY2026 and has no evidence of pull-through.**
Company-reported and unverified: $2.4M of the $5.9M projection is a stocking order from a distributor under a non-binding letter of intent; it ships only on 510(k) clearance, dated Q1 2027, and equals 71,856 cartridges, 42.8 months of the January-September 2026 average, on six months of stability data against a nine-month claim [S1].
:::

Vantelle has six months of cash, company-reported and unverified, and a $30M round that funds its own plan only into 2028. On the report's base — clearance in the second half of 2027, a waiver in 2028 and two to four panels a day — the company consumes $55-70M before breakeven, so $30M is a financing milestone, not the financing. It starts at $6.9M on 2026-09-30 and $1.15M a month [S1]: 6.0 months, exhaustion on 2027-03-30, and $2.3M — 2.0 months — left at the 2027-01-29 target close. That burn is the FY2026E net loss of $14.0M with no capex or working capital in it, so launch spending accelerates it; a close six months late, on 2027-07-29, needs $5.3M of bridge including the first Bluestem payments.

### The plan's operating leverage is real and rests on one variable

| Line item, $M | FY2024 | FY2025 | FY2026E | FY2027P | FY2028P | FY2029P | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Revenue | 1.1 | 2.6 | 5.9 | 16.8 | 41.0 | 78.5 | S1 (unverified) |
| Revenue growth | — | 136% | 127% | 185% | 144% | 91% | S1 (unverified); calculated |
| Gross margin | 49% | 58% | 61% | 63% | 67% | 71% | S1 (unverified) |
| Gross profit | 0.5 | 1.5 | 3.6 | 10.6 | 27.5 | 55.7 | S1 (unverified); calculated |
| Net loss | (9.8) | (12.4) | (14.0) | (16.5) | (6.0) | 9.0 | S1 (unverified) |
| Implied operating cost | 10.3 | 13.9 | 17.6 | 27.1 | 33.5 | 46.7 | S1 (unverified); calculated |

Company-reported and unverified: implied operating cost — gross profit minus net loss — rises from $10.3M in FY2024 to $17.6M in FY2026E and $46.7M in FY2029P while revenue rises 13.3x, and that gap is the investment case. It also sets the target: at the 2029 margin of 71%, breakeven needs $65.8M of revenue — 884 analyzers running 2,400 panels a year at $31, or 660 sites at 1.34 analyzers each, twice the 300 sites targeted

The revenue model is a $2,900 analyzer that costs $3,350 to build and a $38 consumable cartridge it realises $33.40 on, and it only clears its own costs at four to six panels per analyzer per day — four to six times what its 55 evaluation analyzers run. ### The razor loses money twice before the blade earns anything

Each placement is subsidised twice, company-reported and unverified. Build cost is $3,350 against a $2,900 list, and 60% of evaluation sites received their analyzer free, so an average placement realises $1,160 against $3,350 of cost — a $2,190 cash subsidy. The deck does not say how the analyzer is accounted for: the 58% margin needs the $184,250 cost of 55 analyzers outside cost of sales; expensing gives 51%, capitalising 56%. The cartridge earns $17.20 at $33.40 against $16.20 cost, a 51.5% gross margin, less a 3% royalty to Corvia Microfluidics, the 60%-owned affiliate whose 22% minority holder is the chief technology officer; that royalty is $1.00 a cartridge today and $2.35M a year at the 2029 plan — a related-party claim. $7.50 at two million cartridges is a 54% cut from $16.20 on a line running 1,680 a month — a redesign, not a learning curve. Nine sales and support staff placed 55 analyzers in 31 months; at $120,000-240,000 fully loaded and half charged to placements, CAC is $25,600-51,200 [S1]. Three years of cartridge gross profit less the $2,190 subsidy, $15,621, does not repay that; it breaks even at 5.9 panels a day at today's cost and 4.2 at the $7.50 target, where LTV:CAC reaches 3:1.

### 92% reorder is engagement, not demand

Thirty-four of 37 sites reordered within 90 days, company-reported and unverified. The 37 are the sites in the programme at least 90 days; the other four joined later and have not had a 90-day window. What became of the three that did not reorder within 90 days — a later order, lower use or exit — is not disclosed. No site can become a paying commercial customer before clearance, so no lost-deal evidence exists yet; the first will come from the 300-site distributor pipeline. At 41 cartridges a site a month a reorder is one month of consumption: the metric shows repeat use at a price already accepted, not commercial demand. Per site the run rate is 1.35 panels a day against a median of 14 cardiac or metabolic panels sent out daily at the 52 clinics Vantelle surveyed — 10% capture. The plan needs two analyzers at eight panels each, 16 a site, 114% of that median: the model assumes the panel replaces the entire send-out, not the urgent slice. Reaching 300 sites by end-2027 means 259 net adds in twelve months, 21.6 a month against 1.3 a month averaged since March 2024, 402 analyzers and about 1.16M cartridges a year — 57 times the January-September 2026 average of 1,680 — from an 18-person line [S1].

Counter-evidence: evaluation analyzers are investigational, results never reach patient care, and no site has a billing reason to run more. A clinic that collects the full panel reimbursement has an incentive no evaluation site has, and the survey's latent send-out volume makes a modest panel count credible; the plan's is not, until a billing-enabled site demonstrates it. Underwrite panels per analyzer-day, with the site count a milestone, and test the monthly fee against a free-instrument, minimum-volume alternative. Confidence is high on the arithmetic and medium on the interpretation: evaluation data cannot distinguish a floor from a ceiling. Three diligence items: the best evaluation site's monthly volume; the first billing-enabled sites' run rate; and panel mix, since troponin plus potassium alone do not cover a cartridge.

arguments.markdown:
The revenue model is a $2,900 analyzer that costs $3,350 to build and a $38 consumable cartridge it realises $33.40 on, and it only clears its own costs at four to six panels per analyzer per day — four to six times what its 55 evaluation analyzers run. That gap decides whether the $78.5M of 2029 revenue exists. Figures are company-reported and unverified. The only dated volume is 1,680 evaluation cartridges a month, the January-September 2026 average (p.7, headed "2026 average", as of 2026-09-30); across 55 analyzers that is 30.5 cartridge-months, 1.0 panel a day (1.22 on 300 operating days), against 8.0 in 2028 [S1].

### The razor loses money twice before the blade earns anything

Each placement is subsidised twice, company-reported and unverified. Build cost is $3,350 against a $2,900 list, and 60% of evaluation sites received their analyzer free, so an average placement realises $1,160 against $3,350 of cost — a $2,190 cash subsidy. The deck does not say how the analyzer is booked: the 58% margin needs the $184,250 cost of 55 analyzers outside cost of sales; expensing gives 51%, capitalising 56%. The cartridge earns $17.20 at $33.40 against $16.20 cost, a 51.5% gross margin, less a 3% royalty to Corvia Microfluidics, the 60%-owned affiliate whose 22% minority holder is the chief technology officer; that royalty is $1.00 a cartridge today and $2.35M a year at the 2029 plan — a related-party claim. $7.50 at two million cartridges is a 54% cut from $16.20 on a line running 1,680 a month — a redesign, not a learning curve. Nine sales staff placed 55 analyzers in 31 months; at $120,000-240,000 fully loaded and half charged to placements, CAC is $25,600-51,200 [S1]. Three years of cartridge gross profit less the $2,190 subsidy, $15,621, does not repay that; it breaks even at 5.9 panels a day today and 4.2 at the $7.50 target, where LTV:CAC reaches 3:1.

| Line | 2026 actual | 2028 model | 2029 target | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Cartridges per analyzer-month | 30.5 | 200 | 200 | S1 (unverified); calculated |
| Panels per analyzer-day | 1.0 (1.22 on 300 days) | 8.0 | 8.0 | S1 (unverified); calculated |
| Realised cartridge price | $33.40 | $31.00 | $31.00 | S1 (unverified) |
| Cartridge cost | $16.20 | $10.23 | $7.50 | S1 (unverified) |
| Annual cartridge gross profit per analyzer | $5,937 | $47,616 | $54,168 | S1 (unverified); calculated |
| Three-year cartridge LTV less subsidy | $15,621 | $140,658 | $160,314 | S1 (unverified); calculated |
| LTV:CAC, cartridges only | 0.3-0.6x | 2.7-5.5x | 3.1-6.3x | S1 (unverified); calculated |

### FY2025 revenue is three businesses, and its volume is not disclosed

| FY2025 line | Revenue $M | Cost $M (allocated) | Gross margin | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Evaluation: fees and cartridges | 1.10 | 0.33 | 70% | S1 (unverified); calculated |
| Research-use | 0.80 | 0.39 | 51% | S1 (unverified); calculated |
| Contract development | 0.70 | 0.38 | 46% | S1 (unverified) |
| Total | 2.60 | 1.09 | 58% | S1 (unverified) |

FY2025 revenue of $2.6M, company-reported and unverified, is $1.1M evaluation, $0.8M research-use and $0.7M development. The volumes and line costs in the table are reconstructions, not disclosures: at $33.40 and $16.20, $1.10M of evaluation revenue implies about 20,160 cartridges only if the $650 fee were charged on all 55 analyzers for twelve months ($0.43M, an upper bound), and because the 58% is the deck's total, the line costs are allocated back from it — the bridge is an identity, not evidence. Nor does it reconcile with the deck's shipment total: 27,600 cartridges shipped since March 2024 average 890 a month over 31 months, and at the January-September 2026 average of 1,680, nine months consume 15,120, leaving 12,480 — 567 a month — for the 22 months to December 2025. A FY2025 of 20,160 evaluation plus 23,952 research-use cartridges, 44,112, exceeds the entire 27,600. The observed 1.22 panels a day and an FY2025 build of 44,112 cartridges cannot both be true; either the cumulative counts part of the business, the mix is misstated, or the evaluation line carries more than fees and cartridges. Utilisation carries low confidence until a monthly shipment ledger arrives. Normalised FY2026E revenue is $3.5M after removing the $2.4M stocking order: $2.7M in nine months plus $0.8M in Q4; on flat per-analyzer use, the $0.9M increase over FY2025 must come from more analyzers, research-use or development revenue. With the largest customer at 15% and the development partner at 27%, the top two relationships are 42% [S1].

### The clinic's margin rests on the one assay that carries 55% of the payment

CMS's CY2026 Clinical Laboratory Fee Schedule national limitation amounts:

| Test (CPT code) | CY2026 amount | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Troponin, quantitative (84484) | $12.47 | S154; S155; S180 |
| Natriuretic peptide (83880) | $39.26 | S154; S155; S180 |
| Haemoglobin A1c (83036) | $9.71 | S154; S155; S180 |
| Creatinine (82570) | $5.18 | S154; S155; S180 |
| Potassium (84132) | $4.76 | S154; S155; S180 |
| Five-code panel | $71.38 | S154; S155; S180 |

The clinic pays the $38.00 list (p.8); $33.40 is Vantelle's realised price, so a five-code clinic keeps $33.38 and Vantelle takes 47% of the $71.38 payment. The $650 fee equals 19.5 panels of clinic margin: at 30.5 panels a month the clinic grosses $1,018.09 and keeps $368.09, and $7,361.20 at 240 panels — trivial at scale, 64% of the margin at adoption. Natriuretic peptide alone is $39.26, 55% of the payment: four codes without it collect $32.12 and lose $5.88 a cartridge, troponin plus potassium $17.23 and lose $20.77. CMS may cut a test by up to 15% a year in 2027-2029; three such years take the panel to $43.84 and the clinic's spread to $5.84 [S154, S155, S180].

| Product or fee | Price | Per test or analyte | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| Vantelle Q5 cartridge, five assays | $38.00 list; $33.40 realised | $7.60 per analyte at list | S1 (unverified) |
| Vantelle evaluation fee | $650 per analyzer-month | 19.5 panels of clinic margin at observed use | S1 (unverified) |
| Quidel Triage Troponin, 25 tests | $599 | $23.96 | S106 |

### 92% reorder is engagement, not demand

Thirty-four of 37 sites reordered within 90 days, company-reported and unverified. The 37 are sites in the programme at least 90 days; four joined inside 90 days and have not had a window. Whether the three later reordered, cut use or left is not disclosed. No site can become a paying commercial customer before clearance, so no lost-deal evidence exists yet; the first will come from the 300-site distributor pipeline. At 41 cartridges a site a month a reorder is one month of consumption: the metric shows repeat use at a price already accepted, not commercial demand. Per site the run rate is 1.35 panels a day against a median of 14 cardiac or metabolic panels sent out daily at the 52 clinics Vantelle surveyed — 10% capture. The plan needs two analyzers at eight panels each, 16 a site, 114% of that median: the model assumes the panel replaces the entire send-out, not the urgent slice. Reaching 300 sites by end-2027 means 259 net adds in twelve months, 21.6 a month against 1.3 a month averaged since March 2024, 402 analyzers and about 1.16M cartridges a year — 57 times the January-September 2026 average of 1,680 — from an 18-person line [S1].

Counter-evidence: evaluation analyzers are investigational, results never reach patient care, and no site has a billing reason to run more. A clinic that collects the full panel reimbursement has an incentive no evaluation site has, and the survey's latent send-out volume makes a modest panel count credible; the plan's is not, until a billing-enabled site demonstrates it. Underwrite panels per analyzer-day, with the site count a milestone, and test the monthly fee against a free-instrument, minimum-volume alternative. Confidence is high on the arithmetic and medium on the interpretation: evaluation data cannot distinguish a floor from a ceiling. Three diligence items: the best evaluation site's monthly volume; the first billing-enabled sites' run rate; and panel mix, since troponin plus potassium alone do not cover a cartridge.

::: evidence
**A placement runs one panel a day, not eight; at CMS's CY2026 rates the five-code clinic keeps $368.09 a month.** 55 analyzers consumed 1,680 cartridges a month, the January-September 2026 average, company-reported and unverified — 30.5 per analyzer-month against 240; the five-code panel pays $71.38 and the cartridge costs the clinic $38.00, so the panel leaves $33.38 and the $650 fee equals 19.5 panels, and a placement's $15,621 three-year gross profit does not repay an estimated $25,600-51,200 to win it [S1, S154, S180]. The FY2025 line volumes do not reconcile with 27,600 cumulative shipments, so the 58% margin and the 1.22 rate carry low confidence until the shipment ledger arrives.
:::

Professional investment analysis is defined by **specificity**, not length. A 200-page report that uses vague language is worse than a 50-page report where every claim has a number attached. The following standards are non-negotiable:

- ❌ "approximately 45%" → ✅ "43.1373%" or "43.1%" (state source and confidence)

- ❌ "large facility" → ✅ "16,000 m², including GMP plants for Class II and III active medical devices"

### People Must Be Traceable
- ❌ "graduated from a well-known university" → ✅ "BS, University of Science and Technology of China, mechatronic engineering; MS, Hong Kong Polytechnic University, software engineering"
- ❌ "has worked at several companies" → ✅ each role: company + title + dates + specific achievements
- ❌ "industry veteran" → ✅ "69 peer-reviewed papers; previously head of clinical partnerships at Neuralink"

- Every key hire must have: institution + degree + year + prior employer + role + achievements

### Events Must Be Dated
- ❌ "recently completed funding" → ✅ "on 2026-06-26, phase 1 of the super factory was completed and began operating"

### If Data Is Unavailable
- State EXACTLY what is missing (e.g., "registered capital not disclosed" not "insufficient information")

arguments.markdown:
Vantelle has six months of cash, company-reported and unverified, and a $30M round that funds its own plan only into 2028. On the report's base — clearance in the second half of 2027, a waiver in 2028 and two to four panels a day — the company consumes $55-70M before breakeven, so $30M is a financing milestone, not the financing. It starts at $6.9M on 2026-09-30 and $1.15M a month [S1]: 6.0 months, exhaustion on 2027-03-30, and $2.3M — 2.0 months — left at the 2027-01-29 target close. That burn is the FY2026E net loss of $14.0M with no capex or working capital in it, so launch spending accelerates it; a close six months late, on 2027-07-29, needs $5.3M of bridge including the first Bluestem payments.

### The plan's operating leverage is real and rests on one variable

| Line item, $M | FY2024 | FY2025 | FY2026E | FY2027P | FY2028P | FY2029P | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Revenue | 1.1 | 2.6 | 5.9 | 16.8 | 41.0 | 78.5 | S1 (unverified) |
| Revenue growth | — | 136% | 127% | 185% | 144% | 91% | S1 (unverified); calculated |
| Gross margin | 49% | 58% | 61% | 63% | 67% | 71% | S1 (unverified) |
| Gross profit | 0.5 | 1.5 | 3.6 | 10.6 | 27.5 | 55.7 | S1 (unverified); calculated |
| Net loss | (9.8) | (12.4) | (14.0) | (16.5) | (6.0) | 9.0 | S1 (unverified) |
| Implied operating cost | 10.3 | 13.9 | 17.6 | 27.1 | 33.5 | 46.7 | S1 (unverified); calculated |

Company-reported and unverified: implied operating cost — gross profit minus net loss — rises from $10.3M in FY2024 to $17.6M in FY2026E and $46.7M in FY2029P while revenue rises 13.3x, and that gap is the investment case. It also sets the target: at the 2029 margin of 71%, breakeven needs $65.8M of revenue — 884 analyzers running 2,400 panels a year at $31, or 660 sites at 1.34 analyzers each, twice the 300 sites targeted for end-2027. The deck's own $78.5M needs 1,055 analyzers at eight panels a day, 2.6 times the 402 analyzers behind the 300-site plan. The cost target fails the same test: two million cartridges a year is what buys the $7.50 cost; at the 1.22 panels a day the 55 evaluation analyzers ran in the January-September 2026 average, an analyzer consumes 360 cartridges a year, so that volume needs 5,500 analyzers, and the 402 analyzers behind the 300-site plan produce 147,000 cartridges, 7% of it, where the only disclosed cost is $16.20 and the margin 48%, not 76% [S1].

### Forty-one per cent of 2026 revenue cannot be delivered in 2026

Company-reported FY2026E revenue of $5.9M includes a $2.4M opening stocking order from Southwest Clinical Supply that ships only on 510(k) clearance, dated Q1 2027, under a non-binding LOI [S1]. At $33.40 a cartridge it is 71,856 cartridges — 42.8 months at the January-September 2026 average of 1,680 a month — for a product with six months of stability data behind a nine-month claim. Excluding it, FY2026 revenue is $3.5M; with $2.7M booked in nine months the fourth quarter is $0.8M against a $0.9M quarterly average, so the base business is not growing into the year-end. Gross margin makes the same point: 61% in FY2026E is above FY2025's 58% in the year the mix shifts toward a distributor, and a 30% wholesale discount would take the order's margin to 39% and the blend to 52%, cutting gross profit by $0.5M.

### Working capital and the term loan are missing from the use of funds

The launch consumes cash before it produces it, and the deck's use of funds has no working-capital line. At peer working-capital intensity — QuidelOrtho carried 55.7 receivable days and 145 inventory days in FY2025 — 2028 revenue of $41.0M and COGS of $13.5M imply $6.3M of receivables and $2.2-5.4M of inventory at 60-145 days, so $8-12M of working capital against near zero today; on the base's $15.0M of 2028 revenue the need is $3-5M [S1, S22]. The debt compounds the timing: the $5.0M Bluestem term loan is interest-only to 2027-03 and then amortises $166,667 a month for 30 months to 2029-09, with the rate and covenants not disclosed — at 10-12% interest is $42,000-50,000 a month, and debt service after 2027-03 is $210,000 a month, 18% of burn. It amortises whether or not the product is cleared. The $6.0M of bridge notes at 8% cost $40,000 a month and become $6.28M at close, converting at 75% of the $3.2564 round price into 2,571,392 shares, 4.9% of the post-round count.

| Metric | FY2025 | FY2026E | Benchmark | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Net margin | (477%) | (237%) | QuidelOrtho (41.5%) | S1 (unverified), S22 |
| Burn multiple | 8.3x | 4.2x, or 15.6x ex-stocking order | Series B median 1.4x | S1 (unverified), S134 |
| ROE and ROIC | not meaningful | not meaningful | Accumulated deficit above $36.2M against $40.5M of equity raised | S1 (unverified); calculated |
| Receivable days | not disclosed | not disclosed | QuidelOrtho 55.7 days | S22 |
| Inventory days | not disclosed | not disclosed | QuidelOrtho 145 days | S22 |

### The round covers the company's plan only if everything lands on time

In the deck's plan — Q1 2027 clearance, eight panels a day, $78.5M of 2029 revenue — $32.3M at close less 2027 outflows of $25.0M leaves $7.3M, and 2028's $12.0M outflow takes it to negative $4.7M: the trough arrives before the 2029 profit and the shortfall is $8-10M, so the plan needs $40M. That plan is not the report's base. The base assumes one more information cycle on S97's FY2024 average of 139 days total time to decision, putting clearance in H2 2027; revenue is $7.0M, $15.0M and $25.0M in 2027-2029, gross margin 52%, 58% and 63%, and operating cost $24M, $27M and $30M. The losses are $20.4M, $18.3M and $14.3M; with $8M of capex, $3M of working capital and $5M of principal, less $7.5M of depreciation, the cumulative outflow is $61M by end-2029 and $68M to breakeven in 2031: the $55-70M range, against $32.3M at close, leaves $25-38M of new money — a $25-40M round — and 23-32% dilution at half the round price. A downside with clearance in H1 2028 or a refused waiver and one to two panels a day adds a further $40-50M and 35-42% dilution [S1, S97, S140].

| $M | Company plan (Q1 2027, 8 panels/day) | Report base (H2 2027, 2-4 panels/day) | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| Revenue, FY2027 / 2028 / 2029 | 16.8 / 41.0 / 78.5 | 7.0 / 15.0 / 25.0 | S1 (unverified); analyst estimate |
| Cash at close, 2027-01-29 | 32.3 | 32.3 | S1 (unverified); calc. |
| FY2027 outflow | 25.0 | 23.4 | S1 (unverified); calc. |
| FY2028 outflow | 12.0 | 22.3 | S1 (unverified); calc. |
| FY2029 | +9.5 inflow | 15.8 outflow | S1 (unverified); calc. |
| Trough | -4.7 in 2028 | -29.1 at end-2029 | S1 (unverified); calc. |
| Capital to breakeven | 40 | 55-70 | S1 (unverified); calc. |
| Additional beyond the round | 8-10 | 25-38 | S1 (unverified); calc. |

These are capital-intensive instrument economics: growth is bought with placed hardware and funded receivables, so the faster Vantelle sells, the more cash it burns before the cartridge annuity arrives. The variable that moves the outcome is panels per analyzer-day, not sites, price or the clearance date: clearance moves the clock, utilisation sets the level. At $31 a cartridge, the base's $25M of 2029 revenue is 806,000 cartridges — 896 analyzers at three panels a day, 600 sites, twice the 300-site plan — which is why even the base consumes $55-70M. The counter-case is discretionary burn: cutting cost and slowing the site ramp would close most of the gap, and a distributor that finances inventory would remove much of the working-capital need, so the shortfall is about this plan, not survival. Capital efficiency is poor: the burn multiple is 8.3x in FY2025, 4.2x in FY2026E, 15.6x excluding the stocking order and 1.5x in FY2027P on the company plan, against a Series B median near 1.4x; on the base's $7.0M of 2027 revenue and $23.4M outflow it is 6.7x against normalised FY2026 revenue. Revenue per dollar of capital raised is $0.05 in FY2025 on $51.5M, and $0.21 in FY2027P on $81.5M including the round — $4.85 of capital per dollar of 2027 revenue on the company plan and $11.6 on the base. Size the round larger or tranche it on clearance and utilisation, and price for a further financing before breakeven. Diligence: the Bluestem rate, covenants and minimum-cash test; the distributor's payment, return and pricing terms; and the Tempe line's cost and yield at launch volumes. Confidence is high on the arithmetic, medium on the projections, which are unaudited management estimates with no auditor, quarterly statements or covenant disclosure (Source: S1, S22, S134).

::: info danger
**The largest single line of FY2026 revenue cannot be delivered in FY2026 and has no evidence of pull-through.**
Company-reported and unverified: $2.4M of the $5.9M projection is a stocking order from a distributor under a non-binding letter of intent; it ships only on 510(k) clearance, dated Q1 2027, and equals 71,856 cartridges, 42.8 months of the January-September 2026 average, on six months of stability data against a nine-month claim [S1].
:::

{"content":[{"type":"text","text":"## Business Model (business_model, revision 22 by Fundamentals Analyst, 8,964 characters)
Revenue model: per-unit consumables on a razor-and-blade system — a $2,900 analyzer that costs $3,350 to build and a $38 cartridge it realises $33.40 on, and it only clears its own costs at four to six panels per analyzer per day — four to six times what its 55 evaluation analyzers run. That gap decides whether the $78.5M of 2029 revenue exists. Figures are company-reported and unverified. The only dated volume is 1,680 evaluation cartridges a month, the January-September 2026 average (p.7, headed "2026 average", as of 2026-09-30); across 55 analyzers that is 30.5 cartridge-months, 1.0 panel a day (1.22 on 300 operating days), against 8.0 in 2028 [S1].

### The razor loses money twice before the blade earns anything

Under the revenue model each placement is subsidised twice, company-reported and unverified. Build cost is $3,350 against a $2,900 list, and 60% of evaluation sites received their analyzer free, so an average placement realises $1,160 against $3,350 of cost — a $2,190 cash subsidy. The deck does not say how the analyzer is booked: the 58% margin needs the $184,250 cost of 55 analyzers outside cost of sales; expensing gives 51%, capitalising 56%. The cartridge earns $17.20 at $33.40 against $16.20 cost, a 51.5% gross margin, less a 3% royalty to Corvia Microfluidics, the 60%-owned affiliate whose 22% minority holder is the chief technology officer; that royalty is $1.00 a cartridge today and $2.35M a year at the 2029 plan — a related-party claim. $7.50 at two million cartridges is a 54% cut from $16.20 on a line running 1,680 a month — a redesign, not a learning curve. Nine sales staff placed 55 analyzers in 31 months; at $120,000-240,000 fully loaded and half charged to placements, CAC is $25,600-51,200 [S1]. Three years of cartridge gross profit less the $2,190 subsidy, $15,621, does not repay that; it breaks even at 5.9 panels a day today and 4.2 at the $7.50 target, where LTV:CAC reaches 3:1.

FY2025 revenue of $2.6M, company-reported and unverified, is $1.1M evaluation, $0.8M research-use and $0.7M development. {"content":[{"type":"text","text":"## Financial Analysis (financials, revision 11 by Fundamentals Analyst, 8,990 characters)
Vantelle has six months of cash, company-reported and unverified, and a $30M round that funds its own plan only into 2028. On the report's base — clearance in the second half of 2027, a waiver in 2028 and two to four panels a day — the company consumes $55-70M before breakeven, so $30M is a financing milestone, not the financing. It starts at $6.9M on 2026-09-30 and $1.15M a month [S1]: 6.0 months, exhaustion on 2027-03-30, and $2.3M — 2.0 months — left at the 2027-01-29 target close. That burn is the FY2026E net loss of $14.0M with no capex or working capital in it, so launch spending accelerates it; a close six months late, on 2027-07-29, needs $5.3M of bridge including the first Bluestem payments.

### The plan's operating leverage is real and rests on one variable

| Line item, $M | FY2024 | FY2025 | FY2026E | FY2027P | FY2028P | FY2029P | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Revenue | 1.1 | 2.6 | 5.9 | 16.8 | 41.0 | 78.5 | S1 (unverified) |
| Revenue growth | — | 136% | 127% | 185% | 144% | 91% | S1 (unverified); calculated |
| Gross margin | 49% | 58% | 61% | 63% | 67% | 71% | S1 (unverified) |
| Gross profit | 0.5 | 1.5 | 3.6 | 10.6 | 27.5 | 55.7 | S1 (unverified); calculated |
| Net loss | (9.8) | (12.4) | (14.0) | (16.5) | (6.0) | 9.0 | S1 (unverified) |
| Implied operating cost | 10.3 | 13.9 | 17.6 | 27.1 | 33.5 | 46.7 | S1 (unverified); calculated |

Company-reported and unverified: implied operating cost — gross profit minus net loss — rises from $10.3M in FY2024 to $17.6M in FY2026E and $46.7M in FY2029P while revenue rises 13.3x, and that gap is the investment case. It also sets the target: at the 2029 margin of 71%, breakeven needs $65.8M of revenue — 884 analyzers running 2,400 panels a year at $31, or 660 sites at 1.34 analyzers each, twice the 300 sites targeted for end-2027. The deck's own $78.5M needs 1,055 analyzers at eight panels a day, 2.6 times the 402 analyzers behind the 300-site plan. The cost target fails the same test: two million cartridges a year is what buys the $7.50 cost; at the 1.22 panels a day the 55 evaluation analyzers ran in the January-September 2026 average, an analyzer consumes 360 cartridges a year, so that volume needs 5,500 analyzers, and the 402 analyzers behind the 300-site plan produce 147,000 cartridges, 7% of it, where the only disclosed cost is $16.20 and the margin 48%, not 76% [S1].

### Forty-one per cent of 2026 revenue cannot be delivered in 2026

Company-reported FY2026E revenue of $5.9M includes a $2.4M opening stocking order from Southwest Clinical Supply that ships only on 510(k) clearance, dated Q1 2027, under a non-binding LOI [S1]. At $33.40 a cartridge it is 71,856 cartridges — 42.8 months at the January-September 2026 average of 1,680 a month — for a product with six months of stability data behind a nine-month claim. Excluding it, FY2026 revenue is $3.5M; with $2.7M booked in nine months the fourth quarter is $0.8M against a $0.9M quarterly average, so the base business is not growing into the year-end. Gross margin makes the same point: 61% in FY2026E is above FY2025's 58% in the year the mix shifts toward a distributor, and a 30% wholesale discount would take the order's margin to 39% and the blend to 52%, cutting gross profit by $0.5M.

### Working capital and the term loan are missing from the use of funds

The launch consumes cash before it produces it, and the deck's use of funds has no working-capital line. At peer working-capital intensity — QuidelOrtho carried 55.7 receivable days and 145 inventory days in FY2025 — 2028 revenue of $41.0M and COGS of $13.5M imply $6.3M of receivables and $2.2-5.4M of inventory at 60-145 days, so $8-12M of working capital against near zero today; on the base's $15.0M of 2028 revenue the need is $3-5M [S1, S22]. The debt compounds the timing: the $5.0M Bluestem term loan is interest-only to 2027-03 and then amortises $166,667 a month for 30 months to 2029-09, with the rate and covenants not disclosed — at 10-12% interest is $42,000-50,000 a month, and debt service after 2027-03 is $210,000 a month, 18% of burn. It amortises whether or not the product is cleared. The $6.0M of bridge notes at 8% cost $40,000 a month and become $6.28M at close, converting at 75% of the $3.2564 round price into 2,571,392 shares, 4.9% of the post-round count.

### The round covers the company's plan only if everything lands on time

In the deck's plan — Q1 2027 clearance, eight panels a day, $78.5M of 2029 revenue — $32.3M at close less 2027 outflows of $25.0M leaves $7.3M, and 2028's $12.0M outflow takes it to negative $4.7M: the trough arrives before the 2029 profit and the shortfall is $8-10M, so the plan needs $40M. That plan is not the report's base. The base assumes one more information cycle on S97's FY2024 average of 139 days total time to decision, putting clearance in H2 2027; revenue is $7.0M, $15.0M and $25.0M in 2027-2029, gross margin 52%, 58% and 63%, and operating cost $24M, $27M and $30M. The losses are $20.4M, $18.3M and $14.3M; with $8M of capex, $3M of working capital and $5M of principal, less $7.5M of depreciation, the cumulative outflow is $61M by end-2029 and $68M to breakeven in 2031: the $55-70M range, against $32.3M at close, leaves $25-38M of new money — a $25-40M round — and 23-32% dilution at half the round price. A downside with clearance in H1 2028 or a refused waiver and one to two panels a day adds a further $40-50M and 35-42% dilution [S1, S97, S140].

These are capital-intensive instrument economics: growth is bought with placed hardware and funded receivables, so the faster Vantelle sells, the more cash it burns before the cartridge annuity arrives. The variable that moves the outcome is panels per analyzer-day, not sites, price or the clearance date: clearance moves the clock, utilisation sets the level. At $31 a cartridge, the base's $25M of 2029 revenue is 806,000 cartridges — 896 analyzers at three panels a day, 600 sites, twice the 300-site plan — which is why even the base consumes $55-70M. The counter-case is discretionary burn: cutting cost and slowing the site ramp would close most of the gap, and a distributor that finances inventory would remove much of the working-capital need, so the shortfall is about this plan, not survival. Capital efficiency is poor: the burn multiple is 8.3x in FY2025, 4.2x in FY2026E, 15.6x excluding the stocking order and 1.5x in FY2027P on the company plan, against a Series B median near 1.4x; on the base's $7.0M of 2027 revenue and $23.4M outflow it is 6.7x against normalised FY2026 revenue. {"content":[{"type":"text","text":"## Risk Assessment (risk, revision 13 by Red Team Analyst, 8,966 characters)
The investment case breaks on utilisation, not regulation. At the rate Vantelle's own evaluation sites run the panel, every placement destroys value and the ask buys an expected return below the venture hurdle and the risk-free rate. Three risks decide the outcome — utilisation, capillary troponin and the CLIA waiver — and the recommendation prices the last two while assuming the first.

### A placement returns value only above five panels a day

The deck reports 1,680 cartridges a month across 55 analyzers and 1.22 per analyzer operating day against the 8.0 the 2028 model assumes. One customer holds 18 analyzers; the independent comparator is unkind: an academic urgent-care programme at two clinics logged 100,000 results in 38 months across three panel types, 94-132 panels a site-month and 3.1-4.4 a site-day. The base case gives 2-4 panels a day 45% weight — the top of the supported range, not its centre — with 40% bear and 15% bull. The mechanism is the placement: three years of cartridge gross profit at $16.20 cost is $15,621 against an estimated $25,600-51,200 to win a site, four panels a day reaches only 1.1-2.3x LTV:CAC against the 3:1 a direct salesforce needs; 3:1 arrives at 5.9. At observed use each placement destroys $9,979-35,579, so 402 analyzers would consume $4.0-14.3M of the round — which means the plan's 300 sites are a marketing cost, not a franchise. [S1, S148]

### The regulatory clock is a sequence problem, not a date problem

The 2026-08-21 additional-information request restarts FDA's 90-FDA-day review clock only when the December 2026 answer arrives, so clearance cannot precede late March 2027. FDA's FY2025 MDUFA report puts 510(k) total time to decision at 139 days on average in FY2024 against a 124-day goal, with a 112-day goal for FY2025; a December 2026 answer plus 139 days points to mid-May 2027. The 175-day Chemistry figure is database total time, not FDA days. The bear's H2 2027 clearance therefore needs a second information request. A second request pushes the decision into H2 2027 and makes a not-substantially-equivalent decision — a category no section prices — the capital-loss path. The waiver is harder: filed in Q3 2027 on a 150-FDA-day goal it decides in Q1 2028 and mid-2028 with a hold, and no cardiac marker appears among FDA's published 2023-2026 waiver approvals. The unused dual 510(k)-plus-waiver route is faster. I put a 45-55% probability on clearance later than June 2027 and a 30% probability on the waiver being refused or deferred beyond 2029; the FDA letter, a troponin-panel pre-submission answer and a powered pivotal protocol would move both. [S97, S92, S69, S72, S147]

### The pivotal study is the first honest test of the assay

The only clinical evidence is 640 venous samples from 128 patients at one site, with six results excluded for insufficient sample or cartridge error and 96.1% categorical agreement with no direction for the five discordant results. Troponin I runs at 11.8% CV at the 99th-percentile cutoff against the IFCC <10% definition and Abbott's cleared <5.2%, so a true value on the cutoff carries a 95% spread of ±23%. The four-site, 1,150-patient finger-stick study run by clinic staff, due Q2 2027, is the first test of the two variables behind the exclusions. I put a 30-40% probability on it failing to show acceptable agreement at the cutoff and a 15-20% probability of outright failure; failure removes troponin, the chest-pain use case and the $12.47 code, takes 50-65% off equity value and leaves a four-analyte heart-failure product, not the acute-cardiac platform the price assumes. [S1, S68, S70]

### Reimbursement is priced at 2026 rates everywhere in this report

CMS's CY2026 CLFS data file (26CLABQ4, the Q4 release updated October 2026) sets 84484 at $12.47, 83880 at $39.26, 83036 at $9.71, 82570 at $5.18 and 84132 at $4.76 — $71.38 for the five-code panel; CMS governs where third-party republications differ. The preliminary CY2027 schedule cuts 1,171 of 1,528 codes, Chemistry 16%, capped at 15% a year through 2029. At that ceiling the panel falls to $60.67 in 2027 and $43.84 in 2029, and clinic contribution per $33.40 cartridge falls $37.98 to $10.44; the $650 fee then costs 62 panels rather than 17. That is a -15% to -25% equity-value risk, and it compounds with CLIA: until a waiver, the 300 sites planned for end-2027 must be moderate-complexity laboratories. ISO 13485 is uncertified while the QMSR has required an ISO-based system since 2026-02-02. Geopolitics does not bind: buyers are American and the EU is closed until CE marking after 2028. [S149, S154, S155, S179, S71]

### The structure caps the upside, and the scenarios misprice both tails

The 19.96% overhang costs equity; the stack costs more. Corvia's $9.4M put comes off first and the $76.8M stack ($36.3M senior B and B-1, $36.0M participating Series A, $4.5M seed) follows, so the new $30M is flat at 1.00x from a $45.7M exit to $256M and needs $426M for 2x and $596M for 3x; 3x on the $36.28M B-plus-B-1 class needs $568M, against a $100M clearing price for a cleared, waived platform. The bull's $400-500M exit is 4-5x that price, 2.14x at $450M and a 16.4% IRR over five years; $256M returns 1.00x, $350M 1.55x. The bear returns capital: a $50-100M sale covers Bluestem and the B's $30M preference, 1.00x. Weighted 15% bull, 45% base and 40% bear (0.15 × 2.14x + 0.45 × 1.00x + 0.40 × 1.00x), the expected return is 1.17x over 4.5 years, a 3.6% IRR at $140M; at $70M the bull is 3.50x, the base 1.06x, giving 1.40x and 7.8%. [S99, S126, S100]

### Survival is not the same as returns

{"content":[{"type":"text","text":"## Market & Industry Analysis (market, revision 16 by Market Analyst, 8,947 characters)
The company's $2.4B US serviceable-market estimate is an arithmetic artefact of one unproven input: at the 1.22 panels per analyzer per operating day its own 41 evaluation sites delivered in the 2026 year to date, the same 13,200 sites and the same $38 cartridge support $368M of annual revenue, 15% of the claim and 60.7% of Abbott's entire global point-of-care revenue line. The need is real; the number is not. Both the $2.4B and the volume behind it are company-provided, unaudited and not independently confirmed [S1, S67].

The site count survives independent checks and is conservative. The Urgent Care Association counted 15,032 open centers in January 2025, 39% hospital-owned or affiliated and 67% open seven days a week; Definitive Healthcare counted 11,877 active clinics in June 2025; the Journal of Urgent Care Medicine reported 14,245 in September 2024. The deck's 11,400 urgent-care sites sits at the bottom of the range; 1,800 rural hospitals is plausible. Volume is where the file breaks. Deck p.7 heads its column "Cartridges a month, 2026 average": 1,680 across 41 sites and 55 analyzers, 41 a site on p.9, with figures as of 2026-09-30, a 2026 year-to-date average; FY2025 monthly volume is not disclosed. The same page states 27,600 cartridges shipped since March 2024, 890 a month over 31 months. Any FY2025 line split is a reconstruction from the 2026 average and cannot coexist with that cumulative total: 20,160 evaluation plus 23,952 research-use would total 44,112, and 20,160 plus the 15,120 implied by nine months at 1,680 already exceeds 27,600. A residual of 12,480 over the 22 pre-2026 months, 567 a month, follows only if 1,680 held every 2026 month; it is an inference, not a disclosure, and conflicts with the FY2025 line build. Across 55 analyzers, 1,680 is 30.5 cartridges per analyzer-month and 1.22 per operating day at 300 days, or 1.35 per site-day against the model's 8.0, a 6.5x gap that carries low confidence until a shipment ledger arrives. Either billing-enabled clinics run six times more than evaluation sites, or the company needs 1,800 sites at observed utilisation to reach $41.0M; it has 41. Its 52-clinic survey reports a median 14 send-outs a day, a different measure from cartridges used [S79, S80, S78, S1].

A $2.4B SAM for one five-analyte panel would be 17%-83% of every point-of-care test sold in the US. The $368M figure at observed utilisation is 12.7% of the smallest published US point-of-care estimate and 60.7% of Abbott's $606M global point-of-care revenue, which is a revenue line, not a market estimate [S93, S94, S96, S67].

CMS's CY2026 national limitation amounts pay $71.38 for all five codes; without 83880 the other four cap at $32.12, below the $38 list and the $33.40 realised price. {"content":[{"type":"text","text":"## ESG Assessment (esg, revision 8 by Regulatory Analyst, 8,955 characters)
Vantelle's product addresses a real gap in clinic care, but its governance, quality-system and data-handling facts do not yet support a $170M post-money valuation and a $15M lead cheque. Four of six board seats are filled; the Series B seat is Meridian's, the independent seat vacant. Finance has been run by a part-time interim CFO since March 2026; ISO 13485 certification is absent, audit booked Q1 2027; the lead 510(k) has been under an FDA information request since 2026-08-21; and the deck discloses neither the HIPAA business-associate architecture for HL7/FHIR transfer nor the IDE/IRB basis for 41 paid sites. Geopolitics, labour and environment are not material: US-only revenue, 64 employees, a pilot line. Each gap is fixable; together they make the $15M milestone capital, not a Q1 2027 bet. Company figures are unverified. [S1]

### Two founder seats are not the problem; the empty independent seat is

Two founder directors of six is not control. The gap is the vacant independent seat, no disclosed audit committee and a part-time CFO at a company running an FDA submission, waiver study and scale-up. The CFO left in February 2026; the interim has been part-time since March. Cash was $6.9M at 2026-09-30 against $1.15M monthly burn, and the $5.0M Bluestem loan starts 30 principal payments in March 2027, one month after close. The gap is a pricing issue: the controls are thinner than the $170M valuation implies. Require a mutually agreed independent director, an audit committee with a financial expert, a permanent CFO within six months and monthly reporting on cash, FDA correspondence and quality metrics. These figures are company-provided and unverified. [S1]

### The Corvia royalty is small until it meets an exit

The 3% cartridge royalty goes to Corvia, 60% owned by Vantelle, where CTO Dr Tomasz Lindqvist holds 22% — 0.66% of cartridge sales. Every $10M of cartridge revenue carries $300,000 of royalty, $120,000 to the 40% minority and $66,000 to the CTO. The exit is the larger issue: the minority may put its 40% at fair value on an acquisition, $9.4M capitalising 3% of FY2029 plan revenue at 10x. It ranks ahead of the Series B and should reduce the price. Require disinterested approval and a fairness opinion of the royalty and the put, a cap or conversion of the put, and cap-table disclosure. These terms are company-provided and unverified. [S1]

### Quality culture is the open file

ISO 13485 certification is absent and FDA's QMSR has required an ISO 13485-based system since 2026-02-02. The regulatory vice-president who prepared the 510(k) left in September 2025; her successor joined in November 2025, two months before filing. The 2026-08-21 request's content is undisclosed, so the deficiency could be labelling, the 640-sample study or the quality system. FDA's 2024-05-09 warning letter to Cue Health cited unauthorised device changes and lot-release failures, and ordered a stop-sale. A warning letter before clearance would delay launch, complicate the waiver and give 41 clinic customers pause. [S1, S71, S113]

### Patient data has no visible contract

The Q5 sends results to the clinic EHR over Wi-Fi using HL7 and FHIR, making Vantelle a vendor that creates, receives and transmits PHI for a covered entity. Under HHS rules that requires a BAA with each clinic, equivalent terms with subcontractors, Security Rule safeguards and breach reporting; the business associate is directly liable. The deck discloses no BAA count, SOC 2 or HITRUST report, named privacy officer, encryption or incident-response terms, or cyber insurance. Silence is not proof, but it is material non-disclosure at 41 PHI sites. Executed BAAs, a current security report and a named security owner should be closing conditions. [S1, S135]

{"content":[{"type":"text","text":"## Executive Briefing (executive_summary, revision 10 by Lead Analyst, 7,841 characters)
Meridian should not lead Vantelle's Series B at $140M pre-money. The company has the strongest clinical wedge in the file — a five-analyte finger-stick panel aimed at clinics that cannot staff a laboratory, 41 paid evaluation sites and a 92% reorder rate — and a first-of-kind packaging position that incumbents would pay for. It also has the weakest operating proof: 1,680 cartridges a month across 55 analyzers — the January-September 2026 average on deck p.7, with the monthly series and FY2025 volume not disclosed — is 1.22 panels per analyzer operating day against the eight its 2028 plan needs; 27,600 cumulative shipments since March 2024 average 890 a month, so the 2026 rate is roughly double the programme average, and on flat per-analyzer use the $0.9M rise to $3.5M normalised FY2026 revenue has to come from more analyzers, research-use or development revenue, which the deck does not decompose; the financial section's FY2025 split of 20,160 evaluation and 23,952 research-use cartridges is a reconstruction from that 2026 average, and 44,112 FY2025 cartridges cannot coexist with 27,600 shipped to date, so the 1.22 rate and the FY2025 margin bridge carry low confidence until a shipment ledger arrives; troponin runs at 11.8% CV against the IFCC's <10% standard; the 510(k) is under an information request and a CLIA waiver has no cardiac precedent; and $6.9M of cash is six months at the current burn. Evidence confidence is medium on the regulatory calendar and low on the commercial plan, because every operating figure is company-reported and no public record of the company, its 510(k) or its patents exists [S1].

The price is the second problem. Five methods cluster at $50-100M with a $76M midpoint against the $140M ask and $170M post-money. The preference stack totals $76.8M — $30.0M senior B, $6.28M B-1, $36.0M Series A and $4.5M seed — and the Series A then participates at 23.75% of value above it, so the $30M Series B needs $596M of proceeds for 3x and $426M for 2x, while the April 2026 clearing price for a cleared, waived platform was $100M. The company's own 2029 plan, at 2.5x revenue, is worth $196M and returns the new money 1.0x. Only a strategic premium to $400-500M makes the bull case work, and that is 4-5x the clearing price [S126].

The consensus — the company plan, the $8M insider commitment, a Q1 2027 clearance and a 2027 waiver — is not the report's view. We differ on utilisation and price, not on the need: a first billing cohort above six panels a day and a waiver path accepted by FDA would re-rate the asset, while a second information request, a capillary troponin failure or a refused cardiac waiver would take most of the equity value. If Meridian wants exposure before the proofs arrive, the only defensible structure is a lower pre-money, a tranched cheque, a capped Series A participation and a capped or converted Corvia put [S72].

Three risks decide the outcome: utilisation staying near the evaluation rate, the capillary troponin study failing at the cutoff, and a waiver refused or deferred for the cardiac analyte. Each has an early warning in the sensitivity analysis and none is priced at the ask. The immediate financial risk is the runway against a close that still has to be signed, and a base case that consumes more than the round before breakeven.

Before any cheque, Meridian's diligence list should obtain the FDA letter and the pivotal protocol, the Corvia LLC agreement and its change-of-control clause, the Bluestem rate and covenants, the distributor's purchase terms, and the first billing cohort's panels per day and collected revenue per cartridge. Those items, not another meeting with management, decide whether the price is defensible or zero.

{"content":[{"type":"text","text":"## Comprehensive Scoring & Recommendation (scoring, revision 9 by Lead Analyst, 7,921 characters)
Vantelle scores below the threshold for a lead at the ask and inside the range for a wait-for-milestone position. The score is not a verdict on the technology: the need and the team sit in the middle of the scale. It is a verdict on evidence — a product short of its own menu, a regulatory path with no waived cardiac precedent, and unit economics that fail at the company's own utilisation. The recommendation is Wait for milestone: no cheque at the ask, a conditional offer at a lower pre-money, and a re-underwrite when clearance, the waiver pre-submission and the first billing cohort report.

| Dimension | Weight | Score (1-10) | Rationale | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Market need and addressable demand | 15% | 6 | Real clinical need and 41 paying evaluation sites; but the $2.4B SAM is 6.5x observed use, and only the 60.3% traditional urgent-care segment can carry the full-menu economics, which supports $222M | S1 (unverified), S79 |
| Product and technical evidence | 20% | 4 | Five-in-one finger-stick packaging is first-of-kind in the US; troponin at 11.8% CV fails the IFCC <10% benchmark, no capillary data, reader patent on final rejection | S68, S1 (unverified) |
| Regulatory pathway and quality system | 20% | 3 | 2026-08-21 information request pending, 139-day FY2024 average total time to decision against a 124-day goal, no troponin-I waiver precedent, ISO 13485 uncertified | S97, S72, S147, S71 |
| Business model and unit economics | 15% | 3 | 1.22 panels per analyzer-day against 8.0 modelled; three-year LTV $15,621 against $25,600-51,200 CAC; 5.9 panels needed for 3:1 | S1 (unverified), S148 |
| Financial plan and capital efficiency | 10% | 3 | 6.0 months of cash at $1.15M a month; $55-70M needed on the H2 2027 base against a $30M round; $2.4M of FY2026E revenue cannot ship in FY2026 | S1 (unverified) |
| Team and execution | 10% | 5 | Emergency-physician CEO and microfluidics CTO; thin regulatory, quality and finance bench with turnover in 2025-26 | S1 (unverified) |
| Governance and structure | 5% | 4 | 19.96% post-money option overhang, $9.4M Corvia put ahead of the B, part-time interim CFO, independent board seat vacant | S1 (unverified) |
| Valuation and exit | 5% | 2 | $140M ask against a $50-100M methods cluster; $596M needed for 3x against a $100M 2026 clearing price | S1 (unverified), S126 |

The weighted average is 3.9 (0.9 + 0.8 + 0.6 + 0.45 + 0.3 + 0.5 + 0.2 + 0.1) [S1]. Two dimensions can re-rate the company, by less than a single step suggests. A clearance certificate and an accepted waiver pre-submission would lift regulatory from 3 to 6-7, adding 0.6-0.8 points at its 20% weight; a first billing cohort above 5.9 panels a day would lift unit economics from 3 to 7, adding 0.6 points at 15%. Together they add about 1.2-1.4 points, not two per dimension. Conversely, a second information request or a capillary troponin failure takes product and regulatory to 2 and the composite down by about 0.6 points. The asymmetry is why price matters more than the score: on company-reported terms (unverified), the probability-weighted return is 1.17x over 4.5 years at the ask and 1.40x at $70M, a 3.6% versus 7.8% IRR, both below the 25% return Meridian requires of a Series B lead. That gap is why the conditional offer is an option on the milestone, not a return case at either price.

### How the recommendation changes under the downside

The base case carries a 45% weight: clearance in H2 2027, a waiver in 2028-29, 2-4 panels a day and a $150-250M sale in 2031 returning the $30M Series B 1.0x at its preference. The bear case carries 40%: a second request or a capillary-troponin deficiency, a refused or deferred waiver, and a $50-100M distressed sale in 2028 that still covers the $36.3M senior preference on company-reported terms, unverified, and returns 1.0x [S126].

### The branches that change the recommendation

The recommendation becomes Pass if the waiver is refused for the cardiac analyte or the pivotal study misses the cutoff, because both remove the chest-pain use case and 50-65% of equity value. It becomes Invest with conditions at a lower pre-money if clearance arrives and the first billing cohort exceeds four panels a day. It becomes Invest now only if the FDA letter proves documentation-only and a billing cohort prints above six panels — neither of which is in the file today [S68].

### Position sizing and what can be lost

Private company sizing: no capital at the ask. At a lower pre-money, split the cheque between close and clearance, with a follow-on reserve sized to the plan's funding gap rather than to the initial cheque. The maximum loss is not the full commitment: a distressed sale still covers the senior preference, and a full loss needs no sale at all or a price below the preference stack after the Bluestem loan and the Corvia put. The terms that make the cheque worth writing are a board seat, pay-to-play, full pro-rata, a utilisation covenant tied to the second tranche and disinterested approval of the Corvia royalty and put.

### Next diligence and conditions

The diligence list decides the re-underwrite: the FDA information request; the pivotal protocol and any capillary-versus-venous data; the Corvia LLC agreement and the change-of-control clause; the Bluestem rate, covenants and minimum-cash test; the distributor's purchase, payment and return terms; the first billing sites' panels per day and collected revenue per cartridge; and the quality-system certificate. The conditions for any cheque are a price at or below the agreed cap, the tranche structure, the Series A participation capped, the Corvia put capped or converted, a permanent CFO and an independent director before closing, and the certificate before launch. A clearance slip or a later waiver filing reopens the price, not just the timetable.
