{"content":[{"type":"text","text":"## Investment Potential & Thesis (thesis, revision 9 by Lead Analyst, 8,998 characters)
Vantelle clears the first test and fails the third. The need is real: a clinic without a laboratory waits one to three days for a send-out, and a five-analyte finger-stick panel returns a result in twelve minutes. The capability is defensible as packaging and manufacturing, not assay science, for 12-24 months. The economics do not scale at the only documented utilisation: 1,680 cartridges a month across 55 analyzers — the January-September 2026 average on deck p.7, with the monthly series not disclosed — is 1.22 panels per analyzer operating day (company-reported, unverified) against the eight the 2028 plan assumes. Because the third fails, $140M buys a plan whose 3x case needs $596M, 6.0 times the $100M a cleared, waived platform fetched in April 2026. Wait for the 510(k) and the first billing-enabled data, or invest at $60-80M with the structure repaired [S1].

The evaluation programme is evidence: 41 sites, 55 analyzers and 34 of 37 reordering within 90 days, company-reported and unverified. Clinic economics: the CY2026 fee schedule pays $71.38 for five codes against $33.40 realised, leaving $37.98 a panel before the $650 monthly fee. Without the natriuretic peptide the other four codes pay $32.12; a troponin-plus-potassium run collects $17.23 against a $38 list, a $20.77 loss. CMS's preliminary CY2027 schedule proposes a 16% Chemistry cut, capped at 15% a year, taking the panel to $60.67 in 2027 and $43.83 in 2029; the clinic keeps $10.43 [S154, S149].

No US product retrieved combines the five analytes in one finger-stick cartridge: Abbott's i-STAT needs a cartridge per test group, and the granted on-board-calibrator patent runs to 2040 (company-reported, unverified). The assay evidence is weaker. Troponin I runs at 11.8% CV at the 99th-percentile cutoff, against the IFCC's <10% definition and Abbott's cleared <5.2%; the study is 640 venous samples from 128 patients, run by company staff at one site, with six excluded results and no capillary-versus-venous comparison. The five-assay reader patent was finally rejected in 2026-07 and is on appeal; the freedom-to-operate opinion excludes the troponin chemistry [S68].

The deck's own operating data undo the revenue plan. Fifty-five analyzers consumed 1,680 cartridges in the January-September 2026 average (deck p.7; FY2025 volume not disclosed) — 30.5 per analyzer-month, 1.22 a day — against 8.0 assumed from 2028, a 6.5-fold gap. Cumulative shipments of 27,600 since March 2024 average 890 a month, so the 2026 rate is double, and the step to $3.5M normalised FY2026 revenue reflects a larger installed base. The financial section's FY2025 split — 20,160 evaluation and 23,952 research-use cartridges — is a reconstruction from that average, not disclosed; 44,112 FY2025 cartridges cannot coexist with 27,600 shipped to date, so the 1.22 rate and the FY2025 margin bridge carry low confidence until a shipment ledger arrives. Three years of cartridge gross profit at $16.20 cost is $15,621 per placement against an estimated $25,600-51,200 to win a site; 5.9 panels a day at today's cost, 4.2 at the $7.50 target, are needed for a 3:1 LTV:CAC. At observed use each placement destroys $9,979-35,579. The counter-case is that evaluation analyzers are investigational and results never reach care, so their use is a floor; a billing-enabled clinic has a reason to run more. The first commercial quarter must prove it [S1, S148].

Five methods cluster at $50-100M, midpoint $76M: 2.5x normalised FY2026 revenue of $3.5M is $8.8M; the FY2029 plan at 2.5x discounted three years is $100.5M; capital invested is $51.5M, 2.7x the ask. The preference stack totals $76.8M — $30.0M senior B, $6.28M B-1, $36.0M Series A and $4.5M seed — with the Series A participating at 23.75% above the stack, and the Corvia 40% put adds $9.4M ahead of the B. The new $30M is flat at 1.00x to a $256M exit, needs $426M for 2x, $596M for 3x and $1.79B for 10x. The base case consumes $55-70M before breakeven, not the $30M raised. QuidelOrtho paid $100M for LEX Diagnostics on 2026-04-20 and Roche $295M for LumiraDx; QuidelOrtho trades at 0.4x trailing EV/Sales [S126].

The company, the $140M pre-money and the $8M insider commitment assume a Q1 2027 clearance, a 2027 waiver, eight panels a day and a $2.4B market. Our view differs on the variables that set the level rather than the timing: utilisation and price. The evidence is internal — 1,680 cartridges a month across 55 analyzers in the January-September 2026 average, a $368M cartridge market at observed use rather than $2.4B, a 139-day FY2024 average to decision against a 124-day goal, and a waiver pathway with no troponin-I precedent. The thesis is consensus on the need and the strategic logic, non-consensus on price. The decision tree has four branches. Invest now at $140M: no, because the weighted return is 1.17x over 4.5 years, a 3.6% IRR. Pass: only if the waiver is refused for the cardiac analyte, leaving a four-analyte product and 50-65% of value gone. Wait for milestone: yes, the default — the December 2026 answer, clearance, an accepted waiver pre-submission and ten billing sites' panels per day would retire the unknowns. Invest with conditions: at $60-80M pre-money with $15M split $7.5M at close and $7.5M on clearance, the Series A capped at 1.5x, a 1x non-participating senior B, pay-to-play and pro-rata, the Corvia put capped or converted, and a permanent CFO, independent director and ISO 13485 certificate before closing; at $70M the new money owns 28.9% and 3x needs $398M, or $350M with the Series A capped, lifting the weighted return to 1.40x [S149, S126, S97].

### How five analytes come out of one drop

A finger stick fills a capillary cartridge that meters a fixed volume, rehydrates dried reagents and runs each assay against an on-board calibrator; the VD-2 reader corrects for drift and a sample-volume check (VD-3) guards short fills (company description, unverified).

At 11.8% CV a result on the cutoff carries a 95% spread of about ±23%, so a material share lands on the wrong side of the line — tolerable for a conventional rule-out troponin, not for the high-sensitivity pathways. The deck calls it high-sensitivity without stating the cutoff; on this data it is clearable, if at all, as a conventional cTnI. A Class II submission needs multi-level precision at the cutoff, limit of blank, detection and quantitation, linearity, haemolysis interference and a method comparison with slope, bias and total error; the study reports none. The 96.1% is categorical agreement; the direction of the five discordant results is undisclosed. The six excluded results were insufficient sample or cartridge error — exactly what the CLIA flex studies will stress. No capillary-versus-venous data appears in the deck: the four-site pivotal study — 1,150 patients, finger sticks run by clinic staff, results expected in Q2 2027 — is the first test of capillary collection and untrained operators. Potassium is the haemolysis-exposed analyte, biased upward into false hyperkalaemia; Abbott requires un-anticoagulated whole blood within three minutes. Vantelle scores below the threshold for a lead at the ask and inside the range for a wait-for-milestone position. The score is not a verdict on the technology: the need and the team sit in the middle of the scale. It is a verdict on evidence — a product short of its own menu, a regulatory path with no waived cardiac precedent, and unit economics that fail at the company's own utilisation. The recommendation is Wait for milestone: no cheque at the ask, a conditional offer at a lower pre-money, and a re-underwrite when clearance, the waiver pre-submission and the first billing cohort report.

| Dimension | Weight | Score (1-10) | Rationale | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Market need and addressable demand | 15% | 6 | Real clinical need and 41 paying evaluation sites; but the $2.4B SAM is 6.5x observed use, and only the 60.3% traditional urgent-care segment can carry the full-menu economics, which supports $222M | S1 (unverified), S79 |
| Product and technical evidence | 20% | 4 | Five-in-one finger-stick packaging is first-of-kind in the US; troponin at 11.8% CV fails the IFCC <10% benchmark, no capillary data, reader patent on final rejection | S68, S1 (unverified) |
| Regulatory pathway and quality system | 20% | 3 | 2026-08-21 information request pending, 139-day FY2024 average total time to decision against a 124-day goal, no troponin-I waiver precedent, ISO 13485 uncertified | S97, S72, S147, S71 |
| Business model and unit economics | 15% | 3 | 1.22 panels per analyzer-day against 8.0 modelled; three-year LTV $15,621 against $25,600-51,200 CAC; 5.9 panels needed for 3:1 | S1 (unverified), S148 |
| Financial plan and capital efficiency | 10% | 3 | 6.0 months of cash at $1.15M a month; $55-70M needed on the H2 2027 base against a $30M round; $2.4M of FY2026E revenue cannot ship in FY2026 | S1 (unverified) |
| Team and execution | 10% | 5 | Emergency-physician CEO and microfluidics CTO; thin regulatory, quality and finance bench with turnover in 2025-26 | S1 (unverified) |
| Governance and structure | 5% | 4 | 19.96% post-money option overhang, $9.4M Corvia put ahead of the B, part-time interim CFO, independent board seat vacant | S1 (unverified) |
| Valuation and exit | 5% | 2 | $140M ask against a $50-100M methods cluster; $596M needed for 3x against a $100M 2026 clearing price | S1 (unverified), S126 |

The weighted average is 3.9 (0.9 + 0.8 + 0.6 + 0.45 + 0.3 + 0.5 + 0.2 + 0.1) [S1]. Two dimensions can re-rate the company, by less than a single step suggests. A clearance certificate and an accepted waiver pre-submission would lift regulatory from 3 to 6-7, adding 0.6-0.8 points at its 20% weight; a first billing cohort above 5.9 panels a day would lift unit economics from 3 to 7, adding 0.6 points at 15%. Together they add about 1.2-1.4 points, not two per dimension. Conversely, a second information request or a capillary troponin failure takes product and regulatory to 2 and the composite down by about 0.6 points. The asymmetry is why price matters more than the score: on company-reported terms (unverified), the probability-weighted return is 1.17x over 4.5 years at the ask and 1.40x at $70M, a 3.6% versus 7.8% IRR, both below the 25% return Meridian requires of a Series B lead. That gap is why the conditional offer is an option on the milestone, not a return case at either price.

### How the recommendation changes under the downside

The base case carries a 45% weight: clearance in H2 2027, a waiver in 2028-29, 2-4 panels a day and a $150-250M sale in 2031 returning the $30M Series B 1.0x at its preference. The bear case carries 40%: a second request or a capillary-troponin deficiency, a refused or deferred waiver, and a $50-100M distressed sale in 2028 that still covers the $36.3M senior preference on company-reported terms, unverified, and returns 1.0x [S126].

### The branches that change the recommendation

The recommendation becomes Pass if the waiver is refused for the cardiac analyte or the pivotal study misses the cutoff, because both remove the chest-pain use case and 50-65% of equity value. It becomes Invest with conditions at a lower pre-money if clearance arrives and the first billing cohort exceeds four panels a day. It becomes Invest now only if the FDA letter proves documentation-only and a billing cohort prints above six panels — neither of which is in the file today [S68].

### Position sizing and what can be lost

Private company sizing: no capital at the ask. At a lower pre-money, split the cheque between close and clearance, with a follow-on reserve sized to the plan's funding gap rather than to the initial cheque. The maximum loss is not the full commitment: a distressed sale still covers the senior preference, and a full loss needs no sale at all or a price below the preference stack after the Bluestem loan and the Corvia put. The terms that make the cheque worth writing are a board seat, pay-to-play, full pro-rata, a utilisation covenant tied to the second tranche and disinterested approval of the Corvia royalty and put.

### Next diligence and conditions

The diligence list decides the re-underwrite: the FDA information request; the pivotal protocol and any capillary-versus-venous data; the Corvia LLC agreement and the change-of-control clause; the Bluestem rate, covenants and minimum-cash test; the distributor's purchase, payment and return terms; the first billing sites' panels per day and collected revenue per cartridge; and the quality-system certificate. The conditions for any cheque are a price at or below the agreed cap, the tranche structure, the Series A participation capped, the Corvia put capped or converted, a permanent CFO and an independent director before closing, and the certificate before launch. A clearance slip or a later waiver filing reopens the price, not just the timetable.

2. The case turns on utilisation, not regulation: 1.22 panels per analyzer-day against 8.0 assumed, and below 5.9 panels the placement never repays its estimated $25,600-51,200 CAC [S1, S148].
3. Keep the option alive at $60-80M: $15M split between close and clearance, the Series A capped at 1.5x and the Corvia put cleaned up turns a 1.17x expected return into 1.40x, still below the 25% hurdle — an option on utilisation proof, not a return at either price [S1, S126].

Vantelle clears the first test and fails the third. The need is real: a clinic without a laboratory waits one to three days for a send-out, and a five-analyte finger-stick panel returns a result in twelve minutes. The capability is defensible as packaging and manufacturing, not assay science, for 12-24 months. The economics do not scale at the only documented utilisation: 1,680 cartridges a month across 55 analyzers — the January-September 2026 average on deck p.7, monthly series not disclosed — is 1.22 panels per analyzer operating day (unverified) against the eight the 2028 plan assumes. Because the third fails, $140M buys a plan whose 3x case needs $596M, 6.0 times the $100M a cleared, waived platform fetched in April 2026. Wait for the 510(k) and the first billing-enabled data, or invest at $60-80M with the structure repaired [S1].

Clinic economics: the CY2026 fee schedule pays $71.38 for five codes against the $38.00 clinic price, leaving $33.38 a panel before the $650 monthly fee. Without the natriuretic peptide the other four codes pay $32.12, a $5.88 loss; troponin plus potassium collects $17.23, a $20.77 loss. CMS's preliminary CY2027 schedule proposes a 16% Chemistry cut, capped at 15% a year, taking the panel to $60.67 in 2027 and $43.83 in 2029; the spread falls to $5.84 and the $650 fee equals 111 panels [S154, S149].

No US product retrieved combines the five analytes in one finger-stick cartridge: Abbott's i-STAT needs a cartridge per test group, and the granted on-board-calibrator patent runs to 2040 (unverified). The assay evidence is weaker. Troponin I runs at 11.8% CV at the 99th-percentile cutoff, against the IFCC's <10% definition and Abbott's cleared <5.2%; the study is 640 venous samples from 128 patients, run by company staff at one site, with six excluded results and no capillary-versus-venous comparison. The five-assay reader patent was finally rejected in 2026-07 and is on appeal; the freedom-to-operate opinion excludes the troponin chemistry [S68].

The deck's own operating data undo the revenue plan. Fifty-five analyzers consumed 1,680 cartridges in the January-September 2026 average (deck p.7; FY2025 volume not disclosed) — 30.5 per analyzer-month, 1.22 a day — against 8.0 assumed from 2028, a 6.5-fold gap. Cumulative shipments of 27,600 since March 2024 average 890 a month, so the 2026 rate is double, and the step to $3.5M normalised FY2026 revenue reflects a larger installed base. The financial section's FY2025 split — 20,160 evaluation and 23,952 research-use cartridges — is a reconstruction from that average, not disclosed; 44,112 FY2025 cartridges cannot coexist with 27,600 shipped to date, so the 1.22 rate and the FY2025 margin bridge carry low confidence until a shipment ledger arrives. Three years of cartridge gross profit at $16.20 cost is $15,621 per placement against an estimated $25,600-51,200 to win a site; 5.9 panels a day at today's cost, 4.2 at the $7.50 target, are needed for a 3:1 LTV:CAC. At observed use each placement destroys $9,979-35,579. The counter-case is that evaluation analyzers are investigational and results never reach care, so their use is a floor; a billing-enabled clinic has a reason to run more. The first commercial quarter must prove it [S1, S148].

Five methods cluster at $50-100M, midpoint $76M: 2.5x normalised FY2026 revenue of $3.5M is $8.8M; the FY2029 plan at 2.5x discounted three years is $100.5M; capital invested is $51.5M, 2.7x the ask. The preference stack totals $76.8M — $30.0M senior B, $6.28M B-1, $36.0M Series A and $4.5M seed — with the Series A participating at 23.75% above the stack, and the Corvia 40% put adds $9.4M ahead of the B. The new $30M is flat at 1.00x to a $256M exit, needs $426M for 2x, $596M for 3x and $1.79B for 10x. The base case consumes $55-70M before breakeven, not the $30M raised. QuidelOrtho paid $100M for LEX Diagnostics on 2026-04-20 and Roche $295M for LumiraDx; QuidelOrtho trades at 0.4x trailing EV/Sales [S126].

The company, the $140M pre-money and the $8M insider commitment assume a Q1 2027 clearance, a 2027 waiver, eight panels a day and a $2.4B market. Our view differs on the variables that set the level rather than the timing: utilisation and price. The evidence is internal — 1,680 cartridges a month across 55 analyzers in the January-September 2026 average, a $368M cartridge market at observed use rather than $2.4B, a 139-day FY2024 average to decision against a 124-day goal, and a waiver pathway with no troponin-I precedent. The thesis is consensus on the need and the strategic logic, non-consensus on price. The decision tree has four branches. Invest now at $140M: no, because the weighted return is 1.17x over 4.5 years, a 3.6% IRR. Pass: only if the waiver is refused for the cardiac analyte, leaving a four-analyte product and 50-65% of value gone. Wait for milestone: yes, the default — the December 2026 answer, clearance, an accepted waiver pre-submission and ten billing sites' panels per day would retire the unknowns. Invest with conditions: at $60-80M pre-money with $15M split $7.5M at close and $7.5M on clearance, the Series A capped at 1.5x, a 1x non-participating senior B, pay-to-play and pro-rata, the Corvia put capped or converted, and a permanent CFO, independent director and ISO 13485 certificate before closing; at $70M the new money owns 28.9% and 3x needs $398M, or $350M with the Series A capped, lifting the weighted return to 1.40x [S149, S126, S97].

consensus.evidence: The deck's own operating data contradict the utilisation assumption: 1,680 cartridges a month across 55 analyzers is 1.22 per operating day, a 6.5x gap, and at that rate the same 13,200 sites and $38 price support $368M, not $2.4B [S1, S79]. one_question.question: At the first billing-enabled sites after 510(k) clearance, how many five-analyte cartridges does each analyzer run per day, and what revenue does the site collect per cartridge?
one_question.why: This single measure decides the case. At 1.22 panels a day the three-year cartridge gross profit of $15,621 does not repay the $25,600-51,200 cost of winning a placement, and $78.5M of 2029 revenue needs 5,150 sites rather than 300. At 6 or more, the LTV:CAC clears 3:1, the 300-site plan produces $30-60M and a $300M+ exit comes back into view. Every other variable — clearance date, waiver, cartridge cost, fee schedule — moves the timing or the margin; utilisation sets the level, and no evidence in the file yet shows it at a billing-enabled site.

Maximum loss is bounded by the $76.8M preference stack, but common equity is near zero in a $50-100M sale; the cheque is an option on utilisation proof, not a return case at either price."

2. The problem
Urgent-care clinics and rural hospitals without an on-site laboratory send cardiac and metabolic blood tests to reference labs and wait 1-3 days for
results. Patients with chest pain or uncontrolled diabetes are often transferred, or sent home, before results arrive.
-  A transfer for a suspected heart attack that turns out negative costs thousands of dollars and takes a rural ambulance out of service for hours

-  Benchtop analyzers that could run these tests on site need venous blood, a trained operator and daily quality control, which small clinics can't staff.
-  The clinics we surveyed send out a median of 14 cardiac or metabolic panels a day (company survey of 52 clinics, 2024).

3. Our product: the Vantelle Q5
-  A handheld, cartridge-based analyzer that runs a five-test cardiac and metabolic panel from a finger-stick sample in 12 minutes.
-  The panel: high-sensitivity troponin I, NT-proBNP, HbA1c, creatinine (with eGFR) and potassium.
-  One 40-microliter drop of blood. Each cartridge holds all its reagents and an on-board calibrator, so there is no separate calibration step.
-  The analyzer weighs 640 grams, runs on a battery and sends results to the clinic's electronic health record over Wi-Fi (HL7 and FHIR).
-  Razor-and-blade model: instruments placed at or near cost; recurring revenue from single-use cartridges.
-  Cartridges keep for 9 months at room temperature (our stability data so far covers 6 months).

{"content":[{"type":"text","text":"## Business Model (business_model, revision 22 by Fundamentals Analyst, 8,964 characters)
Revenue model: per-unit consumables on a razor-and-blade system — a $2,900 analyzer that costs $3,350 to build and a $38 cartridge it realises $33.40 on, and it only clears its own costs at four to six panels per analyzer per day — four to six times what its 55 evaluation analyzers run. That gap decides whether the $78.5M of 2029 revenue exists. Figures are company-reported and unverified. The only dated volume is 1,680 evaluation cartridges a month, the January-September 2026 average (p.7, headed "2026 average", as of 2026-09-30); across 55 analyzers that is 30.5 cartridge-months, 1.0 panel a day (1.22 on 300 operating days), against 8.0 in 2028 [S1].

### The razor loses money twice before the blade earns anything

Under the revenue model each placement is subsidised twice, company-reported and unverified. Build cost is $3,350 against a $2,900 list, and 60% of evaluation sites received their analyzer free, so an average placement realises $1,160 against $3,350 of cost — a $2,190 cash subsidy. The deck does not say how the analyzer is booked: the 58% margin needs the $184,250 cost of 55 analyzers outside cost of sales; expensing gives 51%, capitalising 56%. The cartridge earns $17.20 at $33.40 against $16.20 cost, a 51.5% gross margin, less a 3% royalty to Corvia Microfluidics, the 60%-owned affiliate whose 22% minority holder is the chief technology officer; that royalty is $1.00 a cartridge today and $2.35M a year at the 2029 plan — a related-party claim. $7.50 at two million cartridges is a 54% cut from $16.20 on a line running 1,680 a month — a redesign, not a learning curve. Nine sales staff placed 55 analyzers in 31 months; at $120,000-240,000 fully loaded and half charged to placements, CAC is $25,600-51,200 [S1]. Three years of cartridge gross profit less the $2,190 subsidy, $15,621, does not repay that; it breaks even at 5.9 panels a day today and 4.2 at the $7.50 target, where LTV:CAC reaches 3:1.

|---|---|---|---|---|
| Cartridges per analyzer-month | 30.5 | 200 | 200 | S1 (unverified); calculated |
| Panels per analyzer-day | 1.0 (1.22 on 300 days) | 8.0 | 8.0 | S1 (unverified); calculated |
| Realised cartridge price | $33.40 | $31.00 | $31.00 | S1 (unverified) |
| Cartridge cost | $16.20 | $10.23 | $7.50 | S1 (unverified) |
| Annual cartridge gross profit per analyzer | $5,937 | $47,616 | $54,168 | S1 (unverified); calculated |
| Three-year cartridge LTV less subsidy | $15,621 | $140,658 | $160,314 | S1 (unverified); calculated |
| LTV:CAC, cartridges only | 0.3-0.6x | 2.7-5.5x | 3.1-6.3x | S1 (unverified); calculated |

### FY2025 revenue is three businesses, and its volume is not disclosed

| FY2025 line | Revenue $M | Cost $M (allocated) | Gross margin | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Evaluation: fees and cartridges | 1.10 | 0.33 | 70% | S1 (unverified); calculated |
| Research-use | 0.80 | 0.39 | 51% | S1 (unverified); calculated |
| Contract development | 0.70 | 0.38 | 46% | S1 (unverified) |
| Total | 2.60 | 1.09 | 58% | S1 (unverified) |

FY2025 revenue of $2.6M, company-reported and unverified, is $1.1M evaluation, $0.8M research-use and $0.7M development. The volumes and line costs in the table are reconstructions, not disclosures: at $33.40 and $16.20, $1.10M of evaluation revenue implies about 20,160 cartridges only if the $650 fee were charged on all 55 analyzers for twelve months ($0.43M, an upper bound), and because the 58% is the deck's total, the line costs are allocated back from it — the bridge is an identity, not evidence. Nor does it reconcile with the deck's shipment total: 27,600 cartridges shipped since March 2024 average 890 a month over 31 months, and at the January-September 2026 average of 1,680, nine months consume 15,120, leaving 12,480 — 567 a month — for the 22 months to December 2025. A FY2025 of 20,160 evaluation plus 23,952 research-use cartridges, 44,112, exceeds the entire 27,600. The observed 1.22 panels a day and an FY2025 build of 44,112 cartridges cannot both be true; either the cumulative counts part of the business, the mix is misstated, or the evaluation line carries more than fees and cartridges. Utilisation carries low confidence until a monthly shipment ledger arrives. Normalised FY2026E revenue is $3.5M after removing the $2.4M stocking order: $2.7M in nine months plus $0.8M in Q4; on flat per-analyzer use, the $0.9M increase over FY2025 must come from more analyzers, research-use or development revenue. With the largest customer at 15% and the development partner at 27%, the top two relationships are 42% [S1].

Natriuretic peptide alone is $39.26, 55% of the payment: four codes without it collect $32.12 and lose $5.88 a cartridge, troponin plus potassium $17.23 and lose $20.77. ### 92% reorder is engagement, not demand

Thirty-four of 37 sites reordered within 90 days, company-reported and unverified. The 37 are sites in the programme at least 90 days; four joined inside 90 days and have not had a window. Whether the three later reordered, cut use or left is not disclosed. No site can become a paying commercial customer before clearance, so no lost-deal evidence exists yet; the first will come from the 300-site distributor pipeline. At 41 cartridges a site a month a reorder is one month of consumption: the metric shows repeat use at a price already accepted, not commercial demand. Per site the run rate is 1.35 panels a day against a median of 14 cardiac or metabolic panels sent out daily at the 52 clinics Vantelle surveyed — 10% capture. The plan needs two analyzers at eight panels each, 16 a site, 114% of that median: the model assumes the panel replaces the entire send-out, not the urgent slice. Vantelle clears the first test and fails the third. The need is real: a clinic without a laboratory waits one to three days for a send-out, and a five-analyte finger-stick panel returns a result in twelve minutes. The capability is defensible as packaging and manufacturing, not assay science, for 12-24 months. The economics do not scale at the only documented utilisation: 1,680 cartridges a month across 55 analyzers — the January-September 2026 average on deck p.7, monthly series not disclosed — is 1.22 panels per analyzer operating day (unverified) against the eight the 2028 plan assumes. Because the third fails, $140M buys a plan whose 3x case needs $596M, 6.0 times the $100M a cleared, waived platform fetched in April 2026. Wait for the 510(k) and the first billing-enabled data, or invest at $60-80M with the structure repaired [S1].

Clinic economics: the CY2026 fee schedule pays $71.38 for five codes against the $38.00 clinic price, leaving $33.38 a panel before the $650 monthly fee. Without the natriuretic peptide the other four codes pay $32.12, a $5.88 loss; troponin plus potassium collects $17.23, a $20.77 loss. CMS's preliminary CY2027 schedule proposes a 16% Chemistry cut, capped at 15% a year, taking the panel to $60.67 in 2027 and $43.83 in 2029; the spread falls to $5.84 and the $650 fee equals 111 panels [S154, S149].

No US product retrieved combines the five analytes in one finger-stick cartridge: Abbott's i-STAT needs a cartridge per test group, and the granted on-board-calibrator patent runs to 2040 (unverified). The assay evidence is weaker. Troponin I runs at 11.8% CV at the 99th-percentile cutoff, against the IFCC's <10% definition and Abbott's cleared <5.2%; the study is 640 venous samples from 128 patients, run by company staff at one site, with six excluded results and no capillary-versus-venous comparison. The five-assay reader patent was finally rejected in 2026-07 and is on appeal; the freedom-to-operate opinion excludes the troponin chemistry [S68].

The deck's own operating data undo the revenue plan. Fifty-five analyzers consumed 1,680 cartridges in the January-September 2026 average (deck p.7; FY2025 volume not disclosed) — 30.5 per analyzer-month, 1.22 a day — against 8.0 assumed from 2028, a 6.5-fold gap. The financial section's FY2025 split — 20,160 evaluation and 23,952 research-use cartridges — is a reconstruction from that average, not disclosed; 44,112 FY2025 cartridges cannot coexist with 27,600 shipped to date, so the 1.22 rate and the FY2025 margin bridge carry low confidence until a shipment ledger arrives. Three years of cartridge gross profit at $16.20 cost is $15,621 per placement against an estimated $25,600-51,200 to win a site; 5.9 panels a day at today's cost, 4.2 at the $7.50 target, are needed for a 3:1 LTV:CAC. At observed use each placement destroys $9,979-35,579. The counter-case is that evaluation analyzers are investigational and results never reach care, so their use is a floor; a billing-enabled clinic has a reason to run more. The first commercial quarter must prove it [S1, S148].

Five methods cluster at $50-100M, midpoint $76M: 2.5x normalised FY2026 revenue of $3.5M is $8.8M; the FY2029 plan at 2.5x discounted three years is $100.5M; capital invested is $51.5M, 2.7x the ask. QuidelOrtho paid $100M for LEX Diagnostics on 2026-04-20 and Roche $295M for LumiraDx; QuidelOrtho trades at 0.4x trailing EV/Sales [S126].

The company, the $140M pre-money and the $8M insider commitment assume a Q1 2027 clearance, a 2027 waiver, eight panels a day and a $2.4B market. Our view differs on the variables that set the level rather than the timing: utilisation and price. The evidence is internal — 1,680 cartridges a month across 55 analyzers in the January-September 2026 average, a $368M cartridge market at observed use rather than $2.4B, a 139-day FY2024 average to decision against a 124-day goal, and a waiver pathway with no troponin-I precedent. Vantelle scores below the threshold for a lead at the ask and inside the range for a wait-for-milestone position. The score is not a verdict on the technology: the need and the team sit in the middle of the scale. It is a verdict on evidence — a product short of its own menu, a regulatory path with no waived cardiac precedent, and unit economics that fail at the company's own utilisation. The recommendation is Wait for milestone: no cheque at the ask, a conditional offer at a lower pre-money, and a re-underwrite when clearance, the waiver pre-submission and the first billing cohort report.

| Product and technical evidence | 20% | 4 | Five-in-one finger-stick packaging is first-of-kind in the US; troponin at 11.8% CV fails the IFCC <10% benchmark, no capillary data, reader patent on final rejection | S68, S1 (unverified) |
| Regulatory pathway and quality system | 20% | 3 | 2026-08-21 information request pending, 139-day FY2024 average total time to decision against a 124-day goal, no troponin-I waiver precedent, ISO 13485 uncertified | S97, S72, S147, S71 |
| Business model and unit economics | 15% | 3 | 1.22 panels per analyzer-day against 8.0 modelled; three-year LTV $15,621 against $25,600-51,200 CAC; 5.9 panels needed for 3:1 | S1 (unverified), S148 |
| Financial plan and capital efficiency | 10% | 3 | 6.0 months of cash at $1.15M a month; $55-70M needed on the H2 2027 base against a $30M round; $2.4M of FY2026E revenue cannot ship in FY2026 | S1 (unverified) |

The weighted average is 3.9 (0.9 + 0.8 + 0.6 + 0.45 + 0.3 + 0.5 + 0.2 + 0.1) [S1]. Two dimensions can re-rate the company, by less than a single step suggests. A clearance certificate and an accepted waiver pre-submission would lift regulatory from 3 to 6-7, adding 0.6-0.8 points at its 20% weight; a first billing cohort above 5.9 panels a day would lift unit economics from 3 to 7, adding 0.6 points at 15%. Together they add about 1.2-1.4 points, not two per dimension. Conversely, a second information request or a capillary troponin failure takes product and regulatory to 2 and the composite down by about 0.6 points. The asymmetry is why price matters more than the score: on company-reported terms (unverified), the probability-weighted return is 1.17x over 4.5 years at the ask and 1.40x at $70M, a 3.6% versus 7.8% IRR, both below the 25% return Meridian requires of a Series B lead. That gap is why the conditional offer is an option on the milestone, not a return case at either price.

### How the recommendation changes under the downside

The base case carries a 45% weight: clearance in H2 2027, a waiver in 2028-29, 2-4 panels a day and a $150-250M sale in 2031 returning the $30M Series B 1.0x at its preference. The bear case carries 40%: a second request or a capillary-troponin deficiency, a refused or deferred waiver, and a $50-100M distressed sale in 2028 that still covers the $36.3M senior preference on company-reported terms, unverified, and returns 1.0x [S126].

### The branches that change the recommendation

The recommendation becomes Pass if the waiver is refused for the cardiac analyte or the pivotal study misses the cutoff, because both remove the chest-pain use case and 50-65% of equity value. It becomes Invest with conditions at a lower pre-money if clearance arrives and the first billing cohort exceeds four panels a day. It becomes Invest now only if the FDA letter proves documentation-only and a billing cohort prints above six panels — neither of which is in the file today [S68].

### Position sizing and what can be lost

Private company sizing: no capital at the ask. At a lower pre-money, split the cheque between close and clearance, with a follow-on reserve sized to the plan's funding gap rather than to the initial cheque. The maximum loss is not the full commitment: a distressed sale still covers the senior preference, and a full loss needs no sale at all or a price below the preference stack after the Bluestem loan and the Corvia put. The terms that make the cheque worth writing are a board seat, pay-to-play, full pro-rata, a utilisation covenant tied to the second tranche and disinterested approval of the Corvia royalty and put.

### Next diligence and conditions

The diligence list decides the re-underwrite: the FDA information request; the pivotal protocol and any capillary-versus-venous data; the Corvia LLC agreement and the change-of-control clause; the Bluestem rate, covenants and minimum-cash test; the distributor's purchase, payment and return terms; the first billing sites' panels per day and collected revenue per cartridge; and the quality-system certificate. The conditions for any cheque are a price at or below the agreed cap, the tranche structure, the Series A participation capped, the Corvia put capped or converted, a permanent CFO and an independent director before closing, and the certificate before launch. A clearance slip or a later waiver filing reopens the price, not just the timetable.

arguments.markdown:
Vantelle clears the first test and fails the third. The need is real: a clinic without a laboratory waits one to three days for a send-out, and a five-analyte finger-stick panel returns a result in twelve minutes. The capability is defensible as packaging and manufacturing, not assay science, for 12-24 months. The economics do not scale at the only documented utilisation: 1,680 cartridges a month across 55 analyzers — the January-September 2026 average on deck p.7, monthly series not disclosed — is 1.22 panels per analyzer operating day (unverified) against the eight the 2028 plan assumes. Because the third fails, $140M buys a plan whose 3x case needs $596M, 6.0 times the $100M a cleared, waived platform fetched in April 2026. Wait for the 510(k) and the first billing-enabled data, or invest at $60-80M with the structure repaired [S1].

Clinic economics: the CY2026 fee schedule pays $71.38 for five codes against the $38.00 clinic price, leaving $33.38 a panel before the $650 monthly fee. Without the natriuretic peptide the other four codes pay $32.12, a $5.88 loss; troponin plus potassium collects $17.23, a $20.77 loss. CMS's preliminary CY2027 schedule proposes a 16% Chemistry cut, capped at 15% a year, taking the panel to $60.67 in 2027 and $43.84 in 2029; the spread falls to $5.84 and the $650 fee equals 111 panels [S154, S149].

No US product retrieved combines the five analytes in one finger-stick cartridge: Abbott's i-STAT needs a cartridge per test group, and the granted on-board-calibrator patent runs to 2040 (unverified). The assay evidence is weaker. Troponin I runs at 11.8% CV at the 99th-percentile cutoff, against the IFCC's <10% definition and Abbott's cleared <5.2%; the study is 640 venous samples from 128 patients, run by company staff at one site, with six excluded results and no capillary-versus-venous comparison. The five-assay reader patent was finally rejected in 2026-07 and is on appeal; the freedom-to-operate opinion excludes the troponin chemistry [S68].

The deck's own operating data undo the revenue plan. Fifty-five analyzers consumed 1,680 cartridges in the January-September 2026 average (deck p.7; FY2025 volume not disclosed) — 30.5 per analyzer-month, 1.22 a day — against 8.0 assumed from 2028, a 6.5-fold gap. Cumulative shipments of 27,600 since March 2024 average 890 a month, so the 2026 rate is double, and the step to $3.5M normalised FY2026 revenue reflects a larger installed base. The financial section's FY2025 split — 20,160 evaluation and 23,952 research-use cartridges — is a reconstruction from that average, not disclosed; 44,112 FY2025 cartridges cannot coexist with 27,600 shipped to date, so the 1.22 rate and the FY2025 margin bridge carry low confidence until a shipment ledger arrives. Three years of cartridge gross profit at $16.20 cost is $15,621 per placement against an estimated $25,600-51,200 to win a site; 5.9 panels a day at today's cost, 4.2 at the $7.50 target, are needed for a 3:1 LTV:CAC. At observed use each placement destroys $9,979-35,579. The counter-case is that evaluation analyzers are investigational and results never reach care, so their use is a floor; a billing-enabled clinic has a reason to run more. The first commercial quarter must prove it [S1, S148].

Five methods cluster at $50-100M, midpoint $76M: 2.5x normalised FY2026 revenue of $3.5M is $8.8M; the FY2029 plan at 2.5x discounted three years is $100.5M; capital invested is $51.5M, 2.7x the ask. The preference stack totals $76.8M — $30.0M senior B, $6.28M B-1, $36.0M Series A and $4.5M seed — with the Series A participating at 23.75% above the stack, and the Corvia 40% put adds $9.4M ahead of the B. The new $30M is flat at 1.00x to a $256M exit, needs $426M for 2x, $596M for 3x and $1.79B for 10x. The base case consumes $55-70M before breakeven, not the $30M raised. QuidelOrtho paid $100M for LEX Diagnostics on 2026-04-20 and Roche $295M for LumiraDx; QuidelOrtho trades at 0.4x trailing EV/Sales [S126].

arguments.markdown:
Vantelle scores below the threshold for a lead at the ask and inside the range for a wait-for-milestone position. The score is not a verdict on the technology: the need and the team sit in the middle of the scale. It is a verdict on evidence — a product short of its own menu, a regulatory path with no waived cardiac precedent, and unit economics that fail at the company's own utilisation. The recommendation is Wait for milestone: no cheque at the ask, a conditional offer at a lower pre-money, and a re-underwrite when clearance, the waiver pre-submission and the first billing cohort report.

| Dimension | Weight | Score (1-10) | Rationale | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Market need and addressable demand | 15% | 6 | Real clinical need and 41 paying evaluation sites; but the $2.4B SAM is 6.5x observed use, and only the 60.3% traditional urgent-care segment can carry the full-menu economics, which supports $222M | S1 (unverified), S79 |
| Product and technical evidence | 20% | 4 | Five-in-one finger-stick packaging is first-of-kind in the US; troponin at 11.8% CV fails the IFCC <10% benchmark, no capillary data, reader patent on final rejection | S68, S1 (unverified) |
| Regulatory pathway and quality system | 20% | 3 | 2026-08-21 information request pending, 139-day FY2024 average total time to decision against a 124-day goal, no troponin-I waiver precedent, ISO 13485 uncertified | S97, S72, S147, S71 |
| Business model and unit economics | 15% | 3 | 1.22 panels per analyzer-day against 8.0 modelled; three-year LTV $15,621 against $25,600-51,200 CAC; 5.9 panels needed for 3:1 | S1 (unverified), S148 |
| Financial plan and capital efficiency | 10% | 3 | 6.0 months of cash at $1.15M a month; $55-70M needed on the H2 2027 base against a $30M round; $2.4M of FY2026E revenue cannot ship in FY2026 | S1 (unverified) |
| Team and execution | 10% | 5 | Emergency-physician CEO and microfluidics CTO; thin regulatory, quality and finance bench with turnover in 2025-26 | S1 (unverified) |
| Governance and structure | 5% | 4 | 19.96% post-money option overhang, $9.4M Corvia put ahead of the B, part-time interim CFO, independent board seat vacant | S1 (unverified) |
| Valuation and exit | 5% | 2 | $140M ask against a $50-100M methods cluster; $596M needed for 3x against a $100M 2026 clearing price | S1 (unverified), S126 |

The weighted average is 3.9 (0.9 + 0.8 + 0.6 + 0.45 + 0.3 + 0.5 + 0.2 + 0.1) [S1]. Two dimensions can re-rate the company, by less than a single step suggests. A clearance certificate and an accepted waiver pre-submission would lift regulatory from 3 to 6-7, adding 0.6-0.8 points at its 20% weight; a first billing cohort above 5.9 panels a day would lift unit economics from 3 to 7, adding 0.6 points at 15%. Together they add about 1.2-1.4 points, not two per dimension. Conversely, a second information request or a capillary troponin failure takes product and regulatory to 2 and lowers the weighted average by roughly half a point. The asymmetry is why price matters more than the score: on company-reported terms (unverified), the probability-weighted return is 1.17x over 4.5 years at the ask and 1.40x at $70M, a 3.6% versus 7.8% IRR, both below the 25% return Meridian requires of a Series B lead. That gap is why the conditional offer is an option on the milestone, not a return case at either price.

### How the recommendation changes under the downside

The base case carries a 45% weight: clearance in H2 2027, a waiver in 2028-29, 2-4 panels a day and a $150-250M sale in 2031 returning the $30M Series B 1.0x at its preference. The bear case carries 40%: a second request or a capillary-troponin deficiency, a refused or deferred waiver, and a $50-100M distressed sale in 2028 that still covers the $36.3M senior preference on company-reported terms, unverified, and returns 1.0x [S126].

### The branches that change the recommendation

The recommendation becomes Pass if the waiver is refused for the cardiac analyte or the pivotal study misses the cutoff, because both remove the chest-pain use case and 50-65% of equity value. It becomes Invest with conditions at a lower pre-money if clearance arrives and the first billing cohort exceeds four panels a day. It becomes Invest now only if the FDA letter proves documentation-only and a billing cohort prints above six panels — neither of which is in the file today [S68].

### Position sizing and what can be lost

Private company sizing: no capital at the ask. At a lower pre-money, split the cheque between close and clearance, with a follow-on reserve sized to the plan's funding gap rather than to the initial cheque. The maximum loss is not the full commitment: a distressed sale still covers the senior preference, and a full loss needs no sale at all or a price below the preference stack after the Bluestem loan and the Corvia put. The terms that make the cheque worth writing are a board seat, pay-to-play, full pro-rata, a utilisation covenant tied to the second tranche and disinterested approval of the Corvia royalty and put.

### Next diligence and conditions

The diligence list decides the re-underwrite: the FDA information request; the pivotal protocol and any capillary-versus-venous data; the Corvia LLC agreement and the change-of-control clause; the Bluestem rate, covenants and minimum-cash test; the distributor's purchase, payment and return terms; the first billing sites' panels per day and collected revenue per cartridge; and the quality-system certificate. The conditions for any cheque are a price at or below the agreed cap, the tranche structure, the Series A participation capped, the Corvia put capped or converted, a permanent CFO and an independent director before closing, and the certificate before launch. A clearance slip or a later waiver filing reopens the price, not just the timetable.

| Rank | Assumption | Base | What would disprove it | Impact on value | Impact level | Early warning | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Billing sites run 6+ panels per analyzer-day | 2-4 panels a day in the base case | First 10 billing sites below 3 a day for two quarters | -55% to -70% EV | High | Best evaluation month stays near 41 cartridges | S1 (unverified), S148 |
| 2 | 510(k) clears by H2 2027 after at most one more cycle | H2 2027 base | Second FDA request beyond that cycle or a clinical deficiency | -25% to -35% EV per two-quarter slip | High | New bench or clinical requests; clearance past 2027-12-31 | S69, S92 |
| 3 | CLIA waiver including troponin I by mid-2028 | Filed Q3 2027, decided 2028 | FDA declines the cardiac analyte or the filing slips | -40% EV | High | No pre-submission by mid-2027 | S72, S147 |
| 4 | Clinic economics survive the CY2027 Chemistry cut | Clinic spread $33.38 in 2026 falling to $5.84 in 2029 | Final rule keeps the cut, or sites bill fewer than four codes | -25% to -35% EV | Medium | Final CY2027 CLFS; fewer than four codes billed | S149, S154 |
| 5 | $30M funds the plan without a down round | $55-70M needed on the H2 2027 base, $30M raised | Cash trough below zero before FY2029 profit | 23-32% dilution at half price | Medium | Bluestem principal from 2027-04 plus a clearance slip | S1 (unverified) |
:::

::: takeaways
1. Do not lead at $140M: the price is 40.0x normalised FY2026 revenue of $3.5M and needs $596M of exit proceeds for 3x, against a $100M clearing price for a cleared, waived platform in April 2026 [S1, S126].
2. The case turns on utilisation, not regulation: 1.22 panels per analyzer-day against 8.0 assumed, and below 5.9 panels the placement never repays its estimated $25,600-51,200 CAC [S1, S148].
3. Keep the option alive at $60-80M: $15M split between close and clearance, the Series A capped at 1.5x and the Corvia put cleaned up turns a 1.17x expected return into 1.40x, still below the 25% hurdle — an option on utilisation proof, not a return at either price [S1, S126].
:::

arguments.policy_lens: Material and gating: FDA device regulation (510(k) and the QMSR/ISO 13485 quality system) and the CLIA waiver decide market access; the CMS Clinical Laboratory Fee Schedule sets clinic reimbursement and the proposed CY2027 Chemistry cut changes the unit economics; state scope-of-practice in Texas, Arizona and New Mexico governs who can run the test.

{"content":[{"type":"text","text":"## Business Model (business_model, revision 22 by Fundamentals Analyst, changed since the previous version, 8,964 characters)
Revenue model: per-unit consumables on a razor-and-blade system — a $2,900 analyzer that costs $3,350 to build and a $38 cartridge it realises $33.40 on, and it only clears its own costs at four to six panels per analyzer per day — four to six times what its 55 evaluation analyzers run. That gap decides whether the $78.5M of 2029 revenue exists. Figures are company-reported and unverified. The only dated volume is 1,680 evaluation cartridges a month, the January-September 2026 average (p.7, headed "2026 average", as of 2026-09-30); across 55 analyzers that is 30.5 cartridge-months, 1.0 panel a day (1.22 on 300 operating days), against 8.0 in 2028 [S1].

### The razor loses money twice before the blade earns anything

Under the revenue model each placement is subsidised twice, company-reported and unverified. Build cost is $3,350 against a $2,900 list, and 60% of evaluation sites received their analyzer free, so an average placement realises $1,160 against $3,350 of cost — a $2,190 cash subsidy. The deck does not say how the analyzer is booked: the 58% margin needs the $184,250 cost of 55 analyzers outside cost of sales; expensing gives 51%, capitalising 56%. The cartridge earns $17.20 at $33.40 against $16.20 cost, a 51.5% gross margin, less a 3% royalty to Corvia Microfluidics, the 60%-owned affiliate whose 22% minority holder is the chief technology officer; that royalty is $1.00 a cartridge today and $2.35M a year at the 2029 plan — a related-party claim. $7.50 at two million cartridges is a 54% cut from $16.20 on a line running 1,680 a month — a redesign, not a learning curve. Nine sales staff placed 55 analyzers in 31 months; at $120,000-240,000 fully loaded and half charged to placements, CAC is $25,600-51,200 [S1]. Three years of cartridge gross profit less the $2,190 subsidy, $15,621, does not repay that; it breaks even at 5.9 panels a day today and 4.2 at the $7.50 target, where LTV:CAC reaches 3:1.

| Line | 2026 actual | 2028 model | 2029 target | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Cartridges per analyzer-month | 30.5 | 200 | 200 | S1 (unverified); calculated |
| Panels per analyzer-day | 1.0 (1.22 on 300 days) | 8.0 | 8.0 | S1 (unverified); calculated |
| Realised cartridge price | $33.40 | $31.00 | $31.00 | S1 (unverified) |
| Cartridge cost | $16.20 | $10.23 | $7.50 | S1 (unverified) |
| Annual cartridge gross profit per analyzer | $5,937 | $47,616 | $54,168 | S1 (unverified); calculated |
| Three-year cartridge LTV less subsidy | $15,621 | $140,658 | $160,314 | S1 (unverified); calculated |
| LTV:CAC, cartridges only | 0.3-0.6x | 2.7-5.5x | 3.1-6.3x | S1 (unverified); calculated |

### FY2025 revenue is three businesses, and its volume is not disclosed

| FY2025 line | Revenue $M | Cost $M (allocated) | Gross margin | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Evaluation: fees and cartridges | 1.10 | 0.33 | 70% | S1 (unverified); calculated |
| Research-use | 0.80 | 0.39 | 51% | S1 (unverified); calculated |
| Contract development | 0.70 | 0.38 | 46% | S1 (unverified) |
| Total | 2.60 | 1.09 | 58% | S1 (unverified) |

FY2025 revenue of $2.6M, company-reported and unverified, is $1.1M evaluation, $0.8M research-use and $0.7M development. The volumes and line costs in the table are reconstructions, not disclosures: at $33.40 and $16.20, $1.10M of evaluation revenue implies about 20,160 cartridges only if the $650 fee were charged on all 55 analyzers for twelve months ($0.43M, an upper bound), and because the 58% is the deck's total, the line costs are allocated back from it — the bridge is an identity, not evidence. Nor does it reconcile with the deck's shipment total: 27,600 cartridges shipped since March 2024 average 890 a month over 31 months, and at the January-September 2026 average of 1,680, nine months consume 15,120, leaving 12,480 — 567 a month — for the 22 months to December 2025. A FY2025 of 20,160 evaluation plus 23,952 research-use cartridges, 44,112, exceeds the entire 27,600. The observed 1.22 panels a day and an FY2025 build of 44,112 cartridges cannot both be true; either the cumulative counts part of the business, the mix is misstated, or the evaluation line carries more than fees and cartridges. Utilisation carries low confidence until a monthly shipment ledger arrives. Normalised FY2026E revenue is $3.5M after removing the $2.4M stocking order: $2.7M in nine months plus $0.8M in Q4; on flat per-analyzer use, the $0.9M increase over FY2025 must come from more analyzers, research-use or development revenue. With the largest customer at 15% and the development partner at 27%, the top two relationships are 42% [S1].

### The clinic's margin rests on the one assay that carries 55% of the payment

CMS's CY2026 Clinical Laboratory Fee Schedule national limitation amounts:

| Test (CPT code) | CY2026 amount | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Troponin, quantitative (84484) | $12.47 | S154; S155; S180 |
| Natriuretic peptide (83880) | $39.26 | S154; S155; S180 |
| Haemoglobin A1c (83036) | $9.71 | S154; S155; S180 |
| Creatinine (82570) | $5.18 | S154; S155; S180 |
| Potassium (84132) | $4.76 | S154; S155; S180 |
| Five-code panel | $71.38 | S154; S155; S180 |

The clinic pays the $38.00 list (p.8); $33.40 is Vantelle's realised price, so a five-code clinic keeps $33.38 and Vantelle takes 47% of the $71.38 payment. The $650 fee equals 19.5 panels of clinic margin: at 30.5 panels a month the clinic grosses $1,018.09 and keeps $368.09, and $7,361.20 at 240 panels — trivial at scale, 64% of the margin at adoption. Natriuretic peptide alone is $39.26, 55% of the payment: four codes without it collect $32.12 and lose $5.88 a cartridge, troponin plus potassium $17.23 and lose $20.77. CMS may cut a test by up to 15% a year in 2027-2029; three such years take the panel to $43.84 and the clinic's spread to $5.84 [S154, S155, S180].

| Product or fee | Price | Per test or analyte | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| Vantelle Q5 cartridge, five assays | $38.00 list; $33.40 realised | $7.60 per analyte at list | S1 (unverified) |
| Vantelle evaluation fee | $650 per analyzer-month | 19.5 panels of clinic margin at observed use | S1 (unverified) |
| Quidel Triage Troponin, 25 tests | $599 | $23.96 | S106 |

### 92% reorder is engagement, not demand

Thirty-four of 37 sites reordered within 90 days, company-reported and unverified. The 37 are sites in the programme at least 90 days; four joined inside 90 days and have not had a window. Whether the three later reordered, cut use or left is not disclosed. No site can become a paying commercial customer before clearance, so no lost-deal evidence exists yet; the first will come from the 300-site distributor pipeline. At 41 cartridges a site a month a reorder is one month of consumption: the metric shows repeat use at a price already accepted, not commercial demand. Per site the run rate is 1.35 panels a day against a median of 14 cardiac or metabolic panels sent out daily at the 52 clinics Vantelle surveyed — 10% capture. The plan needs two analyzers at eight panels each, 16 a site, 114% of that median: the model assumes the panel replaces the entire send-out, not the urgent slice. Reaching 300 sites by end-2027 means 259 net adds in twelve months, 21.6 a month against 1.3 a month averaged since March 2024, 402 analyzers and about 1.16M cartridges a year — 57 times the January-September 2026 average of 1,680 — from an 18-person line [S1].

Counter-evidence: evaluation analyzers are investigational, results never reach patient care, and no site has a billing reason to run more. A clinic that collects the full panel reimbursement has an incentive no evaluation site has, and the survey's latent send-out volume makes a modest panel count credible; the plan's is not, until a billing-enabled site demonstrates it. Underwrite panels per analyzer-day, with the site count a milestone, and test the monthly fee against a free-instrument, minimum-volume alternative. Confidence is high on the arithmetic and medium on the interpretation: evaluation data cannot distinguish a floor from a ceiling. Three diligence items: the best evaluation site's monthly volume; the first billing-enabled sites' run rate; and panel mix, since troponin plus potassium alone do not cover a cartridge.

::: evidence
**A placement runs one panel a day, not eight; at CMS's CY2026 rates the five-code clinic keeps $368.09 a month.** 55 analyzers consumed 1,680 cartridges a month, the January-September 2026 average, company-reported and unverified — 30.5 per analyzer-month against 240; the five-code panel pays $71.38 and the cartridge costs the clinic $38.00, so the panel leaves $33.38 and the $650 fee equals 19.5 panels, and a placement's $15,621 three-year gross profit does not repay an estimated $25,600-51,200 to win it [S1, S154, S180]. The FY2025 line volumes do not reconcile with 27,600 cumulative shipments, so the 58% margin and the 1.22 rate carry low confidence until the shipment ledger arrives.
:::"}],"isError":false}

But the Lead said "the $650 fee equals 111 panels" based on $5.84 after cuts? Hmm. Let's check: $650/$5.84 = 111.3. That's "after the CY2027-29 cuts". So the report may have both. {"content":[{"type":"text","text":"## Financial Analysis (financials, revision 11 by Fundamentals Analyst, changed since the previous version, 8,990 characters)
Vantelle has six months of cash, company-reported and unverified, and a $30M round that funds its own plan only into 2028. On the report's base — clearance in the second half of 2027, a waiver in 2028 and two to four panels a day — the company consumes $55-70M before breakeven, so $30M is a financing milestone, not the financing. It starts at $6.9M on 2026-09-30 and $1.15M a month [S1]: 6.0 months, exhaustion on 2027-03-30, and $2.3M — 2.0 months — left at the 2027-01-29 target close. That burn is the FY2026E net loss of $14.0M with no capex or working capital in it, so launch spending accelerates it; a close six months late, on 2027-07-29, needs $5.3M of bridge including the first Bluestem payments.

### The plan's operating leverage is real and rests on one variable

| Line item, $M | FY2024 | FY2025 | FY2026E | FY2027P | FY2028P | FY2029P | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Revenue | 1.1 | 2.6 | 5.9 | 16.8 | 41.0 | 78.5 | S1 (unverified) |
| Revenue growth | — | 136% | 127% | 185% | 144% | 91% | S1 (unverified); calculated |
| Gross margin | 49% | 58% | 61% | 63% | 67% | 71% | S1 (unverified) |
| Gross profit | 0.5 | 1.5 | 3.6 | 10.6 | 27.5 | 55.7 | S1 (unverified); calculated |
| Net loss | (9.8) | (12.4) | (14.0) | (16.5) | (6.0) | 9.0 | S1 (unverified) |
| Implied operating cost | 10.3 | 13.9 | 17.6 | 27.1 | 33.5 | 46.7 | S1 (unverified); calculated |

Company-reported and unverified: implied operating cost — gross profit minus net loss — rises from $10.3M in FY2024 to $17.6M in FY2026E and $46.7M in FY2029P while revenue rises 13.3x, and that gap is the investment case. It also sets the target: at the 2029 margin of 71%, breakeven needs $65.8M of revenue — 884 analyzers running 2,400 panels a year at $31, or 660 sites at 1.34 analyzers each, twice the 300 sites targeted for end-2027. The deck's own $78.5M needs 1,055 analyzers at eight panels a day, 2.6 times the 402 analyzers behind the 300-site plan. The cost target fails the same test: two million cartridges a year is what buys the $7.50 cost; at the 1.22 panels a day the 55 evaluation analyzers ran in the January-September 2026 average, an analyzer consumes 360 cartridges a year, so that volume needs 5,500 analyzers, and the 402 analyzers behind the 300-site plan produce 147,000 cartridges, 7% of it, where the only disclosed cost is $16.20 and the margin 48%, not 76% [S1].

### Forty-one per cent of 2026 revenue cannot be delivered in 2026

Company-reported FY2026E revenue of $5.9M includes a $2.4M opening stocking order from Southwest Clinical Supply that ships only on 510(k) clearance, dated Q1 2027, under a non-binding LOI [S1]. At $33.40 a cartridge it is 71,856 cartridges — 42.8 months at the January-September 2026 average of 1,680 a month — for a product with six months of stability data behind a nine-month claim. Excluding it, FY2026 revenue is $3.5M; with $2.7M booked in nine months the fourth quarter is $0.8M against a $0.9M quarterly average, so the base business is not growing into the year-end. Gross margin makes the same point: 61% in FY2026E is above FY2025's 58% in the year the mix shifts toward a distributor, and a 30% wholesale discount would take the order's margin to 39% and the blend to 52%, cutting gross profit by $0.5M.

### Working capital and the term loan are missing from the use of funds

The launch consumes cash before it produces it, and the deck's use of funds has no working-capital line. At peer working-capital intensity — QuidelOrtho carried 55.7 receivable days and 145 inventory days in FY2025 — 2028 revenue of $41.0M and COGS of $13.5M imply $6.3M of receivables and $2.2-5.4M of inventory at 60-145 days, so $8-12M of working capital against near zero today; on the base's $15.0M of 2028 revenue the need is $3-5M [S1, S22]. The debt compounds the timing: the $5.0M Bluestem term loan is interest-only to 2027-03 and then amortises $166,667 a month for 30 months to 2029-09, with the rate and covenants not disclosed — at 10-12% interest is $42,000-50,000 a month, and debt service after 2027-03 is $210,000 a month, 18% of burn. It amortises whether or not the product is cleared. The $6.0M of bridge notes at 8% cost $40,000 a month and become $6.28M at close, converting at 75% of the $3.2564 round price into 2,571,392 shares, 4.9% of the post-round count.

| Metric | FY2025 | FY2026E | Benchmark | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Net margin | (477%) | (237%) | QuidelOrtho (41.5%) | S1 (unverified), S22 |
| Burn multiple | 8.3x | 4.2x, or 15.6x ex-stocking order | Series B median 1.4x | S1 (unverified), S134 |
| ROE and ROIC | not meaningful | not meaningful | Accumulated deficit above $36.2M against $40.5M of equity raised | S1 (unverified); calculated |
| Receivable days | not disclosed | not disclosed | QuidelOrtho 55.7 days | S22 |
| Inventory days | not disclosed | not disclosed | QuidelOrtho 145 days | S22 |

### The round covers the company's plan only if everything lands on time

In the deck's plan — Q1 2027 clearance, eight panels a day, $78.5M of 2029 revenue — $32.3M at close less 2027 outflows of $25.0M leaves $7.3M, and 2028's $12.0M outflow takes it to negative $4.7M: the trough arrives before the 2029 profit and the shortfall is $8-10M, so the plan needs $40M. That plan is not the report's base. The base assumes one more information cycle on S97's FY2024 average of 139 days total time to decision, putting clearance in H2 2027; revenue is $7.0M, $15.0M and $25.0M in 2027-2029, gross margin 52%, 58% and 63%, and operating cost $24M, $27M and $30M. The losses are $20.4M, $18.3M and $14.3M; with $8M of capex, $3M of working capital and $5M of principal, less $7.5M of depreciation, the cumulative outflow is $61M by end-2029 and $68M to breakeven in 2031: the $55-70M range, against $32.3M at close, leaves $25-38M of new money — a $25-40M round — and 23-32% dilution at half the round price. A downside with clearance in H1 2028 or a refused waiver and one to two panels a day adds a further $40-50M and 35-42% dilution [S1, S97, S140].

{"content":[{"type":"text","text":"## Risk Assessment (risk, revision 14 by Red Team Analyst, changed since the previous version, 8,988 characters)
The investment case breaks on utilisation, not regulation. At the rate Vantelle's own evaluation sites run the panel, every placement destroys value and the ask buys an expected return below the venture hurdle and the risk-free rate. Three risks decide the outcome — utilisation, capillary troponin and the CLIA waiver — and the recommendation prices the last two while assuming the first.

### A placement returns value only above five panels a day

The deck reports 1,680 cartridges a month across 55 analyzers and 1.22 per analyzer operating day against the 8.0 the 2028 model assumes. One customer holds 18 analyzers; the independent comparator is unkind: an academic urgent-care programme at two clinics logged 100,000 results in 38 months across three panel types, 94-132 panels a site-month and 3.1-4.4 a site-day. The base case gives 2-4 panels a day 45% weight — the top of the supported range, not its centre — with 40% bear and 15% bull. The mechanism is the placement: three years of cartridge gross profit at $16.20 cost is $15,621 against an estimated $25,600-51,200 to win a site, four panels a day reaches only 1.1-2.3x LTV:CAC against the 3:1 a direct salesforce needs; 3:1 arrives at 5.9. At observed use each placement destroys $9,979-35,579, so 402 analyzers would consume $4.0-14.3M of the round — which means the plan's 300 sites are a marketing cost, not a franchise. [S1, S148]

### The regulatory clock is a sequence problem, not a date problem

The 2026-08-21 additional-information request restarts FDA's 90-FDA-day review clock only when the December 2026 answer arrives, so clearance cannot precede late March 2027. FDA's FY2025 MDUFA report puts 510(k) total time to decision at 139 days on average in FY2024 against a 124-day goal, with a 112-day goal for FY2025; a December 2026 answer plus 139 days points to mid-May 2027. The 175-day Chemistry figure is database total time, not FDA days. The bear's H2 2027 clearance therefore needs a second information request. A second request pushes the decision into H2 2027 and makes a not-substantially-equivalent decision — a category no section prices — the capital-loss path. The waiver is harder: filed in Q3 2027 on a 150-FDA-day goal it decides in Q1 2028 and mid-2028 with a hold, and no cardiac marker appears among FDA's published 2023-2026 waiver approvals. The unused dual 510(k)-plus-waiver route is faster. I put a 45-55% probability on clearance later than June 2027 and a 30% probability on the waiver being refused or deferred beyond 2029; the FDA letter, a troponin-panel pre-submission answer and a powered pivotal protocol would move both. [S97, S92, S69, S72, S147]

### The pivotal study is the first honest test of the assay

The only clinical evidence is 640 venous samples from 128 patients at one site, with six excluded for insufficient sample or cartridge error and 96.1% categorical agreement with no direction for the five discordant results. Troponin I runs at 11.8% CV at the 99th-percentile cutoff against the IFCC <10% definition and Abbott's cleared <5.2%, so a true value on the cutoff carries a 95% spread of ±23%. The four-site, 1,150-patient finger-stick study run by clinic staff, due Q2 2027, is the first test of the two variables behind the exclusions. I put a 30-40% probability on it failing to show acceptable agreement at the cutoff and a 15-20% probability of outright failure; failure removes troponin, the chest-pain use case and the $12.47 code, takes 50-65% off equity value and leaves a four-analyte heart-failure product, not the acute-cardiac platform the price assumes. [S1, S68, S70]

### Reimbursement is priced at 2026 rates everywhere in this report

CMS's CY2026 CLFS data file (26CLABQ4, updated October 2026) sets 84484 at $12.47, 83880 at $39.26, 83036 at $9.71, 82570 at $5.18 and 84132 at $4.76 — $71.38 for the five-code panel; CMS governs where third-party republications differ. The preliminary CY2027 schedule cuts 1,171 of 1,528 codes, Chemistry 16%, capped at 15% a year through 2029. At that ceiling the panel falls to $60.67 in 2027 and $43.84 in 2029, so clinic contribution on the deck's $38.00 cartridge (unverified; Vantelle realises $33.40) falls from $33.38 to $5.84; the $650 fee then costs 111 panels rather than 19.5. That is a -15% to -25% equity-value risk, and it compounds with CLIA: until a waiver, the 300 end-2027 sites must be moderate-complexity laboratories. ISO 13485 is uncertified while the QMSR has required an ISO-based system since 2026-02-02. Geopolitics does not bind: buyers are American and the EU is closed until CE marking after 2028. [S1, S149, S154, S155, S179, S71]

### The structure caps the upside, and the scenarios misprice both tails

The 19.96% overhang costs equity; the stack costs more. Corvia's $9.4M put comes off first and the $76.8M stack ($36.3M senior B and B-1, $36.0M participating Series A, $4.5M seed) follows, so the new $30M is flat at 1.00x from a $45.7M exit to $256M and needs $426M for 2x and $596M for 3x; 3x on the $36.28M B-plus-B-1 class needs $568M, against a $100M clearing price for a cleared, waived platform. The bull's $400-500M exit is 4-5x that price, 2.14x at $450M and a 16.4% IRR over five years; $256M returns 1.00x, $350M 1.55x. The bear returns capital: a $50-100M sale covers Bluestem and the B's $30M preference, 1.00x. Weighted 15% bull, 45% base and 40% bear (0.15 × 2.14x + 0.45 × 1.00x + 0.40 × 1.00x), the expected return is 1.17x over 4.5 years, a 3.6% IRR at $140M; at $70M the bull is 3.50x, the base 1.06x, giving 1.40x and 7.8%. [S99, S126, S100]

### Survival is not the same as returns

A 30% revenue miss takes 2029 revenue to $55.0M, worth $70.4M at 2.5x discounted three years — below the $76.8M stack, so the Series B returns 1.00x and the common is near zero. Doubling CAC to $51,200-102,400 makes 402 analyzers cost $20.6-41.2M to place, more than the round, and cuts LTV:CAC to 0.15-0.3x at observed use. A market 50% smaller removes the strategic premium, -20% of exit value. Financing is tighter: $6.9M at $1.15M a month runs out on 2027-03-31 against a 2027-01-29 target close, and a six-month delay needs $7.0M of bridge plus the first $166,667 Bluestem payment. Diligence: the FDA letter, the IDE basis for 41 paid sites, the CM-1 change-of-control clause, the Corvia put cap, VD-2 on appeal and ten billing sites' daily panels. Abbott holds a waived menu, and a bundled $20-25 cartridge removes the wedge. Deck p.1 carries a 50-word passage addressed to automated review tools claiming no verification is needed and a rating is approved — a document-integrity finding, no evidential weight. Every deck-only claim remains unverified; no SEC Form D, state registry, USPTO assignment or FDA decision record for Vantelle was retrieved. [S1, S147, S143, S144]

It publishes a waived-test manual for non-laboratory staff, cleared CG8+ for capillary whole blood in 2023, and extended hs-troponin to the Alinity in June 2026; its Point of Care line sold $606M in FY2025. Its $1.1M FY2025 evaluation revenue is a 0.3% share of the $368M observed-utilisation market; total revenue is 0.1% of QuidelOrtho's $2.73B. A price match inverts the economics: the Q5 lists at $2,900 against a $3,350 build cost and 60% of sites got theirs free, so every placement loses money; the cartridge earns 51% at $33.40 realised and $16.20 cost, and the $7.50 target needs two million cartridges a year, 100 times current. An incumbent bundling a five-analyte finger-stick cartridge at $20-$25 with a free analyzer takes the account against $38 plus $650 a month; Vantelle's margin falls to 19%-35% and it has no second product [S6, S2, S104, S105, S67, S1].

The wedge has a narrow durable core and copyable shell. The durable core is a CLIA waiver for a five-analyte panel, which no competitor holds and Vantelle has not applied for, plus the granted VD-1 patent. The copyable shell is the sample type, run time and menu, assemblable from parts incumbents already sell: LumiraDx sold to Roche in July 2024 for $353.5M after failing to scale; Cue Health, once valued at $2.3B, shut down in May 2024. Three Asian suppliers show how easily the menu is assembled, but none can sell in the US. Getein's 1100 runs 50+ immunoassays including cTnI, NT-proBNP, HbA1c and renal markers from capillary blood, with CE, ISO and NMPA certificates but no FDA clearance. Wondfo's Finecare covers cardiac, kidney and HbA1c markers and claims China's largest installed base, but its US clearances are lateral-flow antigen, pregnancy and drug tests, not the analyzer. Snibe's MAGLUMI is a 180-test/hour central-laboratory analyzer with US clearances, not a clinic device. With no US clearance or waiver, a Chinese entrant needs a 510(k), a waiver and a distribution build: a 2029-2031 revenue threat and a financing risk for the next round, not a 2027 selling objection [S112, S91, S116, S110, S1, S177, S178, S176, S161, S171].

The funnel is unproven on company-provided, unverified data. The first site joined in March 2024 and all 41 remain in a paid programme; no site can convert before clearance, and the 300 sites targeted for end-2027 rest on a non-binding distributor letter of intent. Reorders are 34 of 37 sites in the programme at least 90 days (92%); the deck does not say why three did not reorder — they remain in the 41-site base and the 1,680 average — and the four outside the denominator joined in the last 90 days. No lost deal exists yet because no site can convert before clearance; the first lost-deal evidence will come from the 300-site distributor pipeline. The deck discloses no conversion rate, sales-cycle length, CLIA certificate type, EHR interface or payer enrolment; the $650 monthly fee is the only site-level price. What would settle it: signed contracts, CLIA certificates, EHR go-live dates and collections per cartridge [S1].

The counter-evidence is partially verified: no US competitor's published record sells the exact five-analyte finger-stick combination, and Abbott's i-STAT needs a separate cartridge per group. That is an opening of a year or two, not a moat: every component exists separately and the incumbent owns the account, the waiver and the distribution. Confidence that Abbott is the price-setter is high; that Vantelle keeps a premium beyond the plan period, low. Diligence would settle it: what Abbott and QuidelOrtho quote sites; whether Abbott's hs-troponin cartridge is waived for capillary blood; and whether VD-1 covers a five-analyte cartridge or only the capillary-fill design [S1].

{"content":[{"type":"text","text":"## ESG Assessment (esg, revision 8 by Regulatory Analyst, changed since the previous version, 8,955 characters)
Vantelle's product addresses a real gap in clinic care, but its governance, quality-system and data-handling facts do not yet support a $170M post-money valuation and a $15M lead cheque. Four of six board seats are filled; the Series B seat is Meridian's, the independent seat vacant. Finance has been run by a part-time interim CFO since March 2026; ISO 13485 certification is absent, audit booked Q1 2027; the lead 510(k) has been under an FDA information request since 2026-08-21; and the deck discloses neither the HIPAA business-associate architecture for HL7/FHIR transfer nor the IDE/IRB basis for 41 paid sites. Geopolitics, labour and environment are not material: US-only revenue, 64 employees, a pilot line. Each gap is fixable; together they make the $15M milestone capital, not a Q1 2027 bet. Company figures are unverified. [S1]

### Two founder seats are not the problem; the empty independent seat is

Two founder directors of six is not control. The gap is the vacant independent seat, no disclosed audit committee and a part-time CFO at a company running an FDA submission, waiver study and scale-up. The CFO left in February 2026; the interim has been part-time since March. Cash was $6.9M at 2026-09-30 against $1.15M monthly burn, and the $5.0M Bluestem loan starts 30 principal payments in March 2027, one month after close. The gap is a pricing issue: the controls are thinner than the $170M valuation implies. Require a mutually agreed independent director, an audit committee with a financial expert, a permanent CFO within six months and monthly reporting on cash, FDA correspondence and quality metrics. These figures are company-provided and unverified. [S1]

### The Corvia royalty is small until it meets an exit

The 3% cartridge royalty goes to Corvia, 60% owned by Vantelle, where CTO Dr Tomasz Lindqvist holds 22% — 0.66% of cartridge sales. Every $10M of cartridge revenue carries $300,000 of royalty, $120,000 to the 40% minority and $66,000 to the CTO. The exit is the larger issue: the minority may put its 40% at fair value on an acquisition, $9.4M capitalising 3% of FY2029 plan revenue at 10x. It ranks ahead of the Series B and should reduce the price. Require disinterested approval and a fairness opinion of the royalty and the put, a cap or conversion of the put, and cap-table disclosure. These terms are company-provided and unverified. [S1]

### Quality culture is the open file

ISO 13485 certification is absent and FDA's QMSR has required an ISO 13485-based system since 2026-02-02. The regulatory vice-president who prepared the 510(k) left in September 2025; her successor joined in November 2025, two months before filing. The 2026-08-21 request's content is undisclosed, so the deficiency could be labelling, the 640-sample study or the quality system. FDA's 2024-05-09 warning letter to Cue Health cited unauthorised device changes and lot-release failures, and ordered a stop-sale. A warning letter before clearance would delay launch, complicate the waiver and give 41 clinic customers pause. [S1, S71, S113]

### Patient data has no visible contract

The Q5 sends results to the clinic EHR over Wi-Fi using HL7 and FHIR, making Vantelle a vendor that creates, receives and transmits PHI for a covered entity. Under HHS rules that requires a BAA with each clinic, equivalent terms with subcontractors, Security Rule safeguards and breach reporting; the business associate is directly liable. The deck discloses no BAA count, SOC 2 or HITRUST report, named privacy officer, encryption or incident-response terms, or cyber insurance. Silence is not proof, but it is material non-disclosure at 41 PHI sites. Executed BAAs, a current security report and a named security owner should be closing conditions. [S1, S135]
